skills.name: sam-a2a-agent-design
skills.desc: Design guidance for Solace Agent Mesh remote A2A agents (proxies) — when to connect an external agent vs build an MCP connector or a native agent, agent-card discovery, and auth.
skills.body:
---
name: sam-a2a-agent-design
description: Design guidance for Solace Agent Mesh remote A2A agents (proxies) — when to connect an external agent vs build an MCP connector or a native agent, agent-card discovery, and auth.
---

Design guidance for connecting an **external A2A (agent-to-agent) agent** into the mesh through a proxy.

For the **config schema** see `sam-a2a-agent-schema`.

## What is a remote A2A agent (proxy)?

A proxy connects an external **A2A-over-HTTP agent** — an agent already running outside
this Solace Agent Mesh deployment — into the mesh. It translates between the external agent's A2A/HTTPS
protocol and Agent Mesh's internal A2A/Solace protocol, fetches and publishes the agent's card
to mesh discovery, and forwards tasks with the configured authentication.

Use a proxy when the user wants to integrate an agent hosted elsewhere — a third-party
agent, an agent owned by another team or organization, or an agent running on separate
infrastructure (e.g. an EC2 host, a partner's cloud).

## When to use each — DO NOT confuse these

This is the single most important decision. A bare agent URL most often means an **A2A
proxy**, NOT an MCP connector.

**Remote A2A agent (proxy)** — the user mentions:
- "connect to an external/remote/third-party agent"
- "use the A2A proxy" / "proxy this agent" / "an agent hosted at <URL>"
- an agent that *talks* (accepts tasks and replies), reachable at a base URL
- "another Solace Agent Mesh/A2A agent running somewhere else"

→ Build a **remote A2A agent** (`type: a2a_agent`). Load `sam-a2a-agent-schema`.

**MCP connector** — the user mentions:
- "MCP server", "tool server", "remote tools"
- a server that exposes *tools/functions* for an agent to call (GitHub MCP, Stripe MCP…)
- `streamable-http` or `sse` MCP transport

→ Build an **MCP connector** (`type: connector`). Load `sam-connector-design`.

**Native Solace Agent Mesh agent** — the user wants a brand-new agent built and run *inside* this
deployment (its own instruction, model, tools).

→ Build an **agent** (`type: agent`). Load `sam-agent-design`.

> Decision rule: if the endpoint is *an agent you send tasks to*, it's an A2A proxy. If
> the endpoint *exposes tools/functions* to one of your agents, it's an MCP connector.
> A2A (JSON-RPC over HTTP + agent-card discovery) and MCP are different protocols — an
> MCP connector will NOT work against an A2A agent, and vice versa. When the user says
> "A2A proxy" or "external agent" and gives a base URL, build a remote A2A agent.

## What to gather (Phase 1)

- **Agent URL** — the base URL of the external agent (required).
- **Agent card location** — does it publish a card at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`
  (`well_known`, the common case), at a custom path (`custom` + the URL), or not at all
  (`none` — then ask what skills/capabilities it offers)?
- **Authentication** — does fetching the card and/or sending tasks require auth? Which
  scheme (none, bearer token, API key, basic, OAuth2)? Ask about the *scheme*, not the
  secret values — those use `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>`, which blocks build and test until replaced.
- **Timeout** — only ask if the user expects long-running tasks (default is 120s).
- **A2A version and card signing** — leave `protocolVersion` at `auto` unless the user
  names a version (an agent that misbehaves on A2A 1.0 can be pinned to `v0_3`). Only if
  the user says the agent's card is signed, ask for the JWK Set URL(s) that hold its
  signing keys (`trustedCardJwksUrls`) and whether an unsigned card must be refused
  (`requireSignedCard`).

**Ask the user for the card location and auth scheme (unless they already stated them) —
do not infer them, and do not copy them from another remote A2A agent that already
exists.** Different agents
legitimately use different card locations and auth types, so an existing one is not a
template; `platform_get_component_config` is for avoiding duplicate builds, not for lifting
another agent's auth/card pattern. These two choices set the config's structure (card
location's conditional fields + the discriminated auth object), so guessing wrong yields
an invalid, undeployable config.

A single deployment can run many proxied agents; each remote A2A agent is one external
endpoint.

## Builder workflow

1. Identify the A2A-proxy need during Discovery and confirm it's an external agent, not
   a tool server (MCP) or a new native agent.
2. Generate the remote-agent config artifact (JSON, see `sam-a2a-agent-schema`) with
   `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` for every secret.
3. **Name the outstanding secrets after generating** — do not collect them through
   `ask_user_question`, whose field is not masked. Leave each one as
   `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` and say in your next message which fields are still missing.
   The route open right now — and always — is the user telling you the value in the
   chat, which you write into the artifact with `artifact_search_and_replace_regex`.
   The agent's own page becomes available once it has been saved to the platform: the
   plan-approval flow saves it before it blocks the deploy, a manual Build & Activate
   blocks before saving. The agent can't be deployed until any required auth is
   filled in.
4. A remote A2A agent has no instruction/model/tools to design — its behaviour lives in
   the external agent. Keep the build focused on the connection details.

skills.name: sam-a2a-agent-schema
skills.desc: JSON Schema for a Solace Agent Mesh remote A2A agent (proxy) — fields, agent-card discovery, auth config, and validation rules for connecting an external A2A agent into the mesh.
skills.body:
---
name: sam-a2a-agent-schema
description: JSON Schema for a Solace Agent Mesh remote A2A agent (proxy) — fields, agent-card discovery, auth config, and validation rules for connecting an external A2A agent into the mesh.
---

Configuration schema for a **remote A2A agent** (a.k.a. A2A proxy). A remote agent
connects an external A2A-over-HTTP agent — one hosted outside this Solace Agent Mesh deployment —
into the mesh through a proxy. The proxy translates between the external agent's
A2A/HTTPS protocol and Agent Mesh's internal A2A/Solace protocol.

For **design guidance** (when to build one vs an MCP connector or a native agent) see
`sam-a2a-agent-design`.

## Schema

```json
{{SCHEMA:a2a-agent}}
```

---

## Format

A2A agent artifacts use **JSON** (not YAML) and mirror the `CreateRemoteAgentRequest`
body the platform accepts at `POST /api/v2/platform/remoteAgents`:

```json
{
  "name": "WeatherProxy",
  "description": "Proxies the external weather forecasting agent into the mesh.",
  "agentUrl": "http://ec2-1-2-3-4.compute.amazonaws.com:9000",
  "agentCardLocation": "well_known",
  "agentAuthConfig": { "type": "bearer", "token": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>" }
}
```

**MIME type**: `application/vnd.sam-a2a-agent-config+json`

**Key rules:**
- `name` is required, 3-40 chars, and must be unique among A2A agents.
- `agentUrl` is required and must start with `http://` or `https://` (max 2048 chars).
- `agentCardLocation` is required — one of `well_known`, `custom`, `none`.
- `agentAuthConfig` is required when you are creating the agent — always present, even
  when it needs no auth (`{ "type": "none" }`).
- Use `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` for every secret (bearer token, API key, OAuth client secret).
- **When editing an agent that already exists, leave `agentAuthConfig` as the bare
  `{ "type": "none" }` boilerplate unless you are deliberately changing the credential.**
  The schema above lists it in `required`, so a config without it fails validation —
  omitting it is not an option the tooling allows. It does not need to be: that bare form
  is exactly what this skill tells you to emit, so the save cannot read it as a statement
  about auth and preserves whatever credential is stored.
  What you must not do is write a `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` placeholder or a real secret you
  cannot see — a stored credential reads back redacted, and either of those replaces a
  working one configured elsewhere.
  To genuinely remove auth, set the **top-level** `agentAuthType: "none"`. Removal has to
  be stated there precisely because nothing emits that field by habit, whereas the config
  block's `{ "type": "none" }` is boilerplate.

---

## Agent card discovery (`agentCardLocation`)

The agent card describes the remote agent's name, description, skills, and I/O modes.
How the proxy obtains it:

| Value | Behaviour | Extra fields |
|-------|-----------|--------------|
| `well_known` | Fetch from `{agentUrl}/.well-known/agent-card.json` | none |
| `custom` | Fetch from an explicit URL | `agentCardUrl` **required** |
| `none` | No card published — describe the agent inline | `skills` **required** |

Prefer `well_known` — most A2A agents publish a card there. Only use `none` when the
remote agent has no discoverable card; then supply `skills`, `inputModes`, and
`outputModes` so Solace Agent Mesh can advertise the proxied agent.

---

## Authentication

Auth is a **discriminated object** with a `type` field. There are two independent auth
surfaces:

- **`agentAuthConfig`** (required always; leave it as `{ "type": "none" }` on an edit that
  is not about auth) — credentials sent on every *task request* to the agent.
- **`agentCardAuthConfig`** (optional) — credentials used to *fetch the card*.

Both use the same shape. Pick `type` and fill the matching fields; put secrets behind
`<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>`:

| `type` | Fields |
|--------|--------|
| `none` | `{ "type": "none" }` |
| `bearer` | `{ "type": "bearer", "token": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>" }` |
| `apikey` | `{ "type": "apikey", "apiKey": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>", "headerName": "X-API-Key" }` |
| `basic` | `{ "type": "basic", "username": "...", "password": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>" }` |
| `oauth2` | `{ "type": "oauth2", "tokenEndpoint": "...", "clientId": "...", "clientSecret": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>", "scopes": ["..."] }` |

On a **create**, always include `agentAuthConfig` — use `{ "type": "none" }` when the agent
is unauthenticated. On an **edit**, omit it unless you are changing the credential: a
stored secret reads back redacted, so `{ "type": "none" }` alone is treated as boilerplate
and ignored rather than risk wiping auth someone configured elsewhere.

To genuinely **remove** an existing agent's auth, say so explicitly by setting the
top-level `agentAuthType` as well:

```json
{ "agentAuthType": "none", "agentAuthConfig": { "type": "none" } }
```

---

## Other fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `description` | string | Human description (≤1000 chars). |
| `agentCardHeaders` | object | Extra headers sent when fetching the card. |
| `taskHeaders` | object | Extra headers sent on every task request. |
| `requestTimeoutSeconds` | integer | 10-600; defaults to 120 when omitted. |
| `inputModes` | string[] | e.g. `["text"]`. Only needed when `agentCardLocation: none`. |
| `outputModes` | string[] | e.g. `["text", "file"]`. Only needed when `agentCardLocation: none`. |
| `protocolVersion` | string | A2A version to speak: `auto` (default, the highest both sides support), `v1_0` or `v0_3`. Pin only when the user asks for a version. |
| `trustedCardJwksUrls` | string[] | Up to 10 https URLs (http only on localhost) of JWK Sets whose keys may sign the agent card. A signed card must then verify against them. Not allowed with `agentCardLocation: none`. |
| `requireSignedCard` | boolean | Refuse an unsigned card and send no task until a signed one is accepted. Needs `trustedCardJwksUrls`. Defaults to false. |

---

## Examples

**Well-known card, bearer auth on tasks:**
```json
{
  "name": "ResearchProxy",
  "description": "External research agent exposed through the mesh.",
  "agentUrl": "https://research.partner.example.com",
  "agentCardLocation": "well_known",
  "agentAuthConfig": { "type": "bearer", "token": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>" }
}
```

**Custom card URL, no auth:**
```json
{
  "name": "PublicForecastProxy",
  "description": "Public forecasting agent with a non-standard card path.",
  "agentUrl": "https://forecast.example.com",
  "agentCardLocation": "custom",
  "agentCardUrl": "https://forecast.example.com/a2a/card",
  "agentAuthConfig": { "type": "none" }
}
```

**No card — skills described inline:**
```json
{
  "name": "LegacyProxy",
  "description": "Legacy A2A agent that does not publish a card.",
  "agentUrl": "http://legacy.internal:9000",
  "agentCardLocation": "none",
  "agentAuthConfig": { "type": "none" },
  "skills": [
    { "name": "Summarize", "description": "Summarizes documents." }
  ],
  "inputModes": ["text"],
  "outputModes": ["text"]
}
```

---

## Placeholder convention

Use `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` for every secret (tokens, API keys, client secrets) and for
any required value not provided in the conversation. The UI detects the placeholder and
prompts for the real value before saving.
skills.bodyMd:
Configuration schema for a **remote A2A agent** (a.k.a. A2A proxy). A remote agent
connects an external A2A-over-HTTP agent — one hosted outside this Solace Agent Mesh deployment —
into the mesh through a proxy. The proxy translates between the external agent's
A2A/HTTPS protocol and Agent Mesh's internal A2A/Solace protocol.

For **design guidance** (when to build one vs an MCP connector or a native agent) see
`sam-a2a-agent-design`.

## Schema

```json
{{SCHEMA:a2a-agent}}
```

---

## Format

A2A agent artifacts use **JSON** (not YAML) and mirror the `CreateRemoteAgentRequest`
body the platform accepts at `POST /api/v2/platform/remoteAgents`:

```json
{
  "name": "WeatherProxy",
  "description": "Proxies the external weather forecasting agent into the mesh.",
  "agentUrl": "http://ec2-1-2-3-4.compute.amazonaws.com:9000",
  "agentCardLocation": "well_known",
  "agentAuthConfig": { "type": "bearer", "token": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>" }
}
```

**MIME type**: `application/vnd.sam-a2a-agent-config+json`

**Key rules:**
- `name` is required, 3-40 chars, and must be unique among A2A agents.
- `agentUrl` is required and must start with `http://` or `https://` (max 2048 chars).
- `agentCardLocation` is required — one of `well_known`, `custom`, `none`.
- `agentAuthConfig` is required when you are creating the agent — always present, even
  when it needs no auth (`{ "type": "none" }`).
- Use `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` for every secret (bearer token, API key, OAuth client secret).
- **When editing an agent that already exists, leave `agentAuthConfig` as the bare
  `{ "type": "none" }` boilerplate unless you are deliberately changing the credential.**
  The schema above lists it in `required`, so a config without it fails validation —
  omitting it is not an option the tooling allows. It does not need to be: that bare form
  is exactly what this skill tells you to emit, so the save cannot read it as a statement
  about auth and preserves whatever credential is stored.
  What you must not do is write a `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` placeholder or a real secret you
  cannot see — a stored credential reads back redacted, and either of those replaces a
  working one configured elsewhere.
  To genuinely remove auth, set the **top-level** `agentAuthType: "none"`. Removal has to
  be stated there precisely because nothing emits that field by habit, whereas the config
  block's `{ "type": "none" }` is boilerplate.

---

## Agent card discovery (`agentCardLocation`)

The agent card describes the remote agent's name, description, skills, and I/O modes.
How the proxy obtains it:

| Value | Behaviour | Extra fields |
|-------|-----------|--------------|
| `well_known` | Fetch from `{agentUrl}/.well-known/agent-card.json` | none |
| `custom` | Fetch from an explicit URL | `agentCardUrl` **required** |
| `none` | No card published — describe the agent inline | `skills` **required** |

Prefer `well_known` — most A2A agents publish a card there. Only use `none` when the
remote agent has no discoverable card; then supply `skills`, `inputModes`, and
`outputModes` so Solace Agent Mesh can advertise the proxied agent.

---

## Authentication

Auth is a **discriminated object** with a `type` field. There are two independent auth
surfaces:

- **`agentAuthConfig`** (required always; leave it as `{ "type": "none" }` on an edit that
  is not about auth) — credentials sent on every *task request* to the agent.
- **`agentCardAuthConfig`** (optional) — credentials used to *fetch the card*.

Both use the same shape. Pick `type` and fill the matching fields; put secrets behind
`<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>`:

| `type` | Fields |
|--------|--------|
| `none` | `{ "type": "none" }` |
| `bearer` | `{ "type": "bearer", "token": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>" }` |
| `apikey` | `{ "type": "apikey", "apiKey": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>", "headerName": "X-API-Key" }` |
| `basic` | `{ "type": "basic", "username": "...", "password": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>" }` |
| `oauth2` | `{ "type": "oauth2", "tokenEndpoint": "...", "clientId": "...", "clientSecret": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>", "scopes": ["..."] }` |

On a **create**, always include `agentAuthConfig` — use `{ "type": "none" }` when the agent
is unauthenticated. On an **edit**, omit it unless you are changing the credential: a
stored secret reads back redacted, so `{ "type": "none" }` alone is treated as boilerplate
and ignored rather than risk wiping auth someone configured elsewhere.

To genuinely **remove** an existing agent's auth, say so explicitly by setting the
top-level `agentAuthType` as well:

```json
{ "agentAuthType": "none", "agentAuthConfig": { "type": "none" } }
```

---

## Other fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `description` | string | Human description (≤1000 chars). |
| `agentCardHeaders` | object | Extra headers sent when fetching the card. |
| `taskHeaders` | object | Extra headers sent on every task request. |
| `requestTimeoutSeconds` | integer | 10-600; defaults to 120 when omitted. |
| `inputModes` | string[] | e.g. `["text"]`. Only needed when `agentCardLocation: none`. |
| `outputModes` | string[] | e.g. `["text", "file"]`. Only needed when `agentCardLocation: none`. |
| `protocolVersion` | string | A2A version to speak: `auto` (default, the highest both sides support), `v1_0` or `v0_3`. Pin only when the user asks for a version. |
| `trustedCardJwksUrls` | string[] | Up to 10 https URLs (http only on localhost) of JWK Sets whose keys may sign the agent card. A signed card must then verify against them. Not allowed with `agentCardLocation: none`. |
| `requireSignedCard` | boolean | Refuse an unsigned card and send no task until a signed one is accepted. Needs `trustedCardJwksUrls`. Defaults to false. |

---

## Examples

**Well-known card, bearer auth on tasks:**
```json
{
  "name": "ResearchProxy",
  "description": "External research agent exposed through the mesh.",
  "agentUrl": "https://research.partner.example.com",
  "agentCardLocation": "well_known",
  "agentAuthConfig": { "type": "bearer", "token": "<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>" }
}
```

**Custom card URL, no auth:**
```json
{
  "name": "PublicForecastProxy",
  "description": "Public forecasting agent with a non-standard card path.",
  "agentUrl": "https://forecast.example.com",
  "agentCardLocation": "custom",
  "agentCardUrl": "https://forecast.example.com/a2a/card",
  "agentAuthConfig": { "type": "none" }
}
```

**No card — skills described inline:**
```json
{
  "name": "LegacyProxy",
  "description": "Legacy A2A agent that does not publish a card.",
  "agentUrl": "http://legacy.internal:9000",
  "agentCardLocation": "none",
  "agentAuthConfig": { "type": "none" },
  "skills": [
    { "name": "Summarize", "description": "Summarizes documents." }
  ],
  "inputModes": ["text"],
  "outputModes": ["text"]
}
```

---

## Placeholder convention

Use `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` for every secret (tokens, API keys, client secrets) and for
any required value not provided in the conversation. The UI detects the placeholder and
prompts for the real value before saving.

---
name: sam-agent-schema
description: JSON Schema for Solace Agent Mesh agent configuration — all fields, types, defaults, and examples.
---

Solace Agent Mesh agent configuration schema and practical guide. Every field in an agent's `app_config` is defined below, along with valid values, field interactions, and common patterns.

For **tool details** see `sam-tool-schema`. For **design guidance** see `sam-agent-design`.

## Schema

```yaml
{{SCHEMA:agent}}
```

---

## 1. Identity Fields

Note: System fields (`namespace`, `model`, `display_name`, `session_service`, `artifact_service`, `agent_card_publishing`, `agent_discovery`) are injected by the platform at deployment time and must not be included in generated configs. The one model setting you do write is `model_provider` (section 2).

```yaml
agent_name: my_agent          # Required. Unique ID for broker topics/routing. Use snake_case.
description: "..."             # Required. Free text description of the agent.
version: "1.0"                 # Optional semver string.
agent_type: standard           # "standard" (default) or "workflow" (used by workflow engine).
```

The platform sets `agent_type`; the Builder does not save it.

**Rules:**
- `agent_name` must be unique across the deployment. Convention: `snake_case`, no hyphens.
- For platform-deployed agents, the name is auto-generated as `agent_<uuid>` with underscores.

---

## 2. LLM Model Configuration

### Which model an agent uses: `model_provider`

An agent's model is bound by `model_provider`, a key **inside `app_config`**. It holds the name (the alias on the Models page) of a model the platform has configured:

```yaml
apps:
  - name: my_agent
    app_config:
      agent_name: my_agent
      model_provider: ["planning"]
```

- Get the names from `platform_list_components` with `component_type: model`. Use a chat model; a decision model is refused. A name that is not configured is refused by the save and by the preview.
- Give one entry. The platform binds one model per agent, so a list of two, an empty name, or a value that is not a name is refused.
- Leave `model_provider` out to use the platform default on a new agent. On an existing agent, leaving it out keeps the model the agent already has; `model_provider: []` returns it to the platform default.
- To change the model of an existing agent, edit its artifact and set `app_config.model_provider`. Nothing else changes the model.
- **Never write `model:`**, with a name (`model: general`), a provider string (`model: "openai/gpt-4o"`) or the object form. The platform never reads it, so the agent would stay on its old model. The save and `validate_component_config` refuse it, whether it sits in `app_config` or beside it on the `apps[]` item; so is `model_provider` written beside `app_config` instead of inside it. When the user names a model by its provider string (for example `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`) and no listed name is clearly that model, ask which listed name they mean, or tell them to add one on the Models page: the Builder cannot create models.

### Runtime config files (`sam run`), not the Builder

A hand-written config file that the platform does not generate sets the model with `model:`. Two forms are supported:

#### Simple string form
```yaml
model: "openai/gpt-4o"
```

#### Object form (for custom endpoints)
```yaml
model:
  model: "anthropic/claude-4-5-sonnet"
  api_base: "${LLM_SERVICE_ENDPOINT}"
  api_key: "${LLM_SERVICE_API_KEY}"
  cache_strategy: "5m"         # "none", "5m", "1h" (default "5m")
```

#### Model string format
Format: `"provider/model-name"` — the provider prefix tells the LLM client which API format to use.

**Supported providers and common models:**

| Provider | Example models |
|----------|---------------|
| `openai` | `openai/gpt-4o`, `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, `openai/o3-mini` |
| `anthropic` | `anthropic/claude-4-5-sonnet`, `anthropic/claude-4-5-haiku` |
| `google` | `google/gemini-3.6-flash`, `google/gemini-3.5-flash`, `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` |
| `vertex` | `vertex/gemini-3.5-flash` |
| `bedrock` | `bedrock/anthropic.claude-v2` |
| `azure` | `azure/gpt-4o` (requires api_base pointing to Azure endpoint) |
| `cohere` | `cohere/command-r-plus` |
| `mistral` | `mistral/mistral-large-latest` |
| `groq` | `groq/llama-3.1-70b-versatile` |
| `perplexity` | `perplexity/llama-3.1-sonar-large-128k-online` |
| `ollama` | `ollama/llama3.1` (requires local api_base) |
| `xai` | `xai/grok-2` |
| `openrouter` | `openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.1-405b-instruct` |

**Critical rules:**
- For `openai/` models (which cover any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), `api_base` is either a base URL or the provider's complete chat-completions URL. With a base URL, the client appends `/v1/chat/completions`, dropping one trailing `/v1` from the base first. If the provider does not serve its API under `/v1`, give the complete URL, whose path ends in `/chat/completions` (for example `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/v3/chat/completions`); the client calls it exactly as written. Models that accept a request only through the OpenAI Responses API (the `-pro` models, and some GPT-5 models when the request includes tools) do not work with the complete form.
- In a runtime config file, use env vars: `${LLM_SERVICE_ENDPOINT}`, `${LLM_SERVICE_API_KEY}`, `${LLM_SERVICE_GENERAL_MODEL_NAME}`.

### LLM control parameters
```yaml
supports_streaming: false      # Platform default.
max_tokens: 0                  # 0 = the model's own output ceiling for Claude 5.x on the Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex and Azure providers, otherwise the provider default. Set only if you need to limit output.
# max_llm_calls_per_task: 30   # Model calls per task; 30 is the default. Uncomment and set about 60 only for an agent that gathers data and then builds a document (deck, report).
enable_auto_continuation: true # Allow the agent to continue if response is truncated.
```

The Builder saves every key in this schema. Leaving a key out keeps the agent's stored value; to remove a stored `output_schema`, a setting or a block, write the key with `null`. A value such as `output_schema` is replaced whole, not merged. A key the platform manages (`agent_type`, `internal`, `required_scopes`, `skills_base_path`, `skills_cache_path`, `volumes`, `networks`, and `allow_loopback` inside a built-in tool's `tool_config`) is not saved by the Builder: the save keeps the stored value and warns once if you state one. `null` removes a stored setting with two exceptions: peer access needs `allow_list: []`, and the platform-managed keys cannot be removed from the Builder.

**About `max_llm_calls_per_task`:** a positive whole number is saved with the agent and deployed as written. Zero, a negative number, a fraction or text is refused, and nothing is saved until it is fixed. Leaving the key out of an update keeps the stored limit, and `null` removes it, so the agent runs with the default of 30.

**About `supports_streaming`:** leave it out unless the agent must advertise streaming; a new agent runs with `false`.

---

## 3. Instruction (System Prompt)

```yaml
instruction: |
  You are a security auditor agent...
```

The instruction is the most important field for agent quality. See the `sam-agent-design` skill for the full five-section writing guide. Key points:

- Use YAML block scalar (`|`) for multi-line instructions.
- Structure: Role → Expertise → Guidelines → Constraints → Skill references.
- Keep under ~2000 tokens. Move reference material into skills.
- For interactive agents: include tone/personality guidance and when to ask for clarification.
- For autonomous agents: explicitly state "do not ask for clarification" and describe fallback behavior.

### Injection flags
```yaml
inject_current_time: true          # Stamps each user turn with weekday, date, time and IANA zone
inject_system_purpose: false       # Prepends Solace Agent Mesh platform purpose statement
inject_response_format: false      # Prepends response format guidance
inject_user_profile: false         # Prepends user profile info (enterprise)
```

These are rarely needed — most agents should set their own context in the instruction.

---

## 4. Agent Card (Discovery Identity)

**Required for every agent.** Without an agent card, the agent is invisible to entrypoints and peer agents.

```yaml
agent_card:
  description: "Analyzes code for security vulnerabilities and generates compliance reports."
  version: "1.0"
  defaultInputModes: [text]           # What the agent accepts: text, file, data
  defaultOutputModes: [text, file]    # What the agent produces: text, file, data
  skills:                             # Capabilities (NOT knowledge-bundle skills)
    - id: code-review
      name: Code Review
      description: >-
        Review code for security vulnerabilities, performance issues,
        and coding standard violations.
      tags: [security, code-quality]
      examples:
        - "Review this Python file for SQL injection vulnerabilities"
        - "Check this API endpoint for authentication issues"
    - id: compliance-report
      name: Compliance Reporting
      description: >-
        Generate SOC2, PCI-DSS, and HIPAA compliance reports.
  provider:
    organization: "My Company"
    url: "https://example.com"
```

**Important distinctions:**
- `agent_card.skills` = **capabilities** advertised for discovery (A2A protocol term). These are what the entrypoint and peer agents match against when routing tasks.
- `skills` (top-level) = **knowledge-bundle skills** (directories with reference docs). Completely different concept, confusingly similar name.

**Writing good capability descriptions:**
- Each skill.description should be specific enough that the entrypoint can match a user request to it.
- Include keywords the user would naturally use when asking for this capability.
- Keep descriptions non-overlapping across skills on the same agent.
- Bad: `"Does stuff with code."` — Good: `"Reviews Python code for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities with file paths and remediation steps."`

**Input/output modes:**
- `text` — plain text messages (almost always included)
- `file` — file uploads (input) or file artifacts (output)
- `data` — structured data (JSON, CSV, etc.)

---

## 5. Tool Groups and Individual Tools

### Built-in tool groups

Use `tool_type: builtin-group` to add all tools in a named group:

```yaml
tools:
  - tool_type: builtin-group
    group_name: artifact_management
```

{{TOOL_GROUPS_TABLE}}

### Individual built-in tools

Use `tool_type: builtin` when you need only specific tools or per-tool configuration:

```yaml
tools:
  - tool_type: builtin
    tool_name: web_request
    hil:
      require_approval: true
      approval_message: "This will make an HTTP request."
      timeout: "5m"
      show_args: true
```

### Secure Tool Runtime-backed builtin tools

Tools that ship with Solace Agent Mesh but run out-of-process in the Secure Tool Runtime
(e.g. `mermaid_diagram_generator`, `create_chart_from_plotly_config`,
`execute_python_code`, `ffmpeg`, `pptx_*`) are declared the same way as
in-process builtins when a built-in group registers them. A tool that no built-in group
registers cannot be saved by the Builder under `tool_type: builtin`: a skill's tools
(`xlsx_read`, `docx_create_document`) come with the skill listed under `skills:`, a
connector's runtime (`execute_sql_query`, `graph_db_query`, `slack`) comes with a
connector linked to the agent, and a custom tool ships in an uploaded toolset.

A save that sets `required_scopes` or `auth` on a built-in entry is refused; remove them from the entry.
A save that sets `effect` on a built-in entry is refused as well, because the platform cannot store it and dropping it would loosen the tool's effect classification.

The custom-tool form below is for runtime config files; the Builder does not save it:

```yaml
tools:
  - tool_type: builtin
    tool_name: analyze_data
    tool_description: "Analyzes dataset and produces statistical summary."
    sandbox_profile: standard         # restrictive | standard | permissive
    parameters:
      dataset:
        type: artifact
        description: "The CSV dataset to analyze"
        required: true
      output_format:
        type: string
        description: "Output format: 'summary' or 'detailed'"
        required: false
        default: "summary"
```

**Sandbox profiles:**
- `restrictive` — 512MB RAM, 60s CPU, network isolated. For pure computation.
- `standard` — 1GB RAM, 300s CPU, network access. Default.
- `permissive` — 4GB RAM, 600s CPU, full access. For heavy processing.

**Special parameter types:**
- `artifact` — accepts an artifact filename as input
- `artifact_list` — accepts a list of artifact filenames

### MCP tools (Model Context Protocol)

```yaml
tools:
  - tool_type: mcp
    connection_params:
      type: stdio                      # stdio | sse | streamable-http
      command: "npx"
      args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres"]
      env:
        DATABASE_URL: "${DATABASE_URL}"
    allow_list: [query, list_tables]   # Only expose these tools (optional)
```

**Transport types:**
- `stdio` — local process (command + args). Most common for development.
- `sse` — Server-Sent Events remote server (url required).
- `streamable-http` — HTTP streaming remote server (url required).

**Tool filtering** (mutually exclusive):
- `tool_name` — expose exactly one tool
- `tool_name_prefix` — expose tools matching prefix
- `allow_list` — expose only listed tools
- `deny_list` — expose all except listed tools

**Effect** (optional, per entry): every tool is `read_only` or `side_effecting`, and an MCP tool is `side_effecting` unless told otherwise. A tool is read_only only if all three hold: it cannot change anything outside the run, whatever its input; it fetches no URL chosen by its input or by the content of a file it reads; it writes, deletes or replaces no artifact under a filename chosen by its caller or by the tool itself. The run is the one task that called the tool, and changing something outside it means writing, sending, deleting, posting, publishing or indexing in an external system, another session or user scope, or starting a job. Changing the run's own session, such as the skills it has loaded, is not outside it. A filename is chosen by the caller when it comes from a parameter, and by the tool when its code fixes or derives it, including a name set on a data object it returns. A result the runtime itself saves under a fresh filename it picks, which it does only when a tool returns data with no name set (auto-disposition), is not a write. Sending the caller's query to one fixed external service, as a search or lookup does, is not fetching a chosen URL. Every other tool is side_effecting. `effect: side_effecting` marks every tool the entry registers side-effecting; `read_only` is not accepted. `trust_annotations: true` lets the server's own `readOnlyHint: true` make its tools `read_only` only when the server also sends `openWorldHint: false` (an omitted `openWorldHint` counts as `true`, the MCP default) and no `destructiveHint: true`; you vouch that such tools meet all three conditions of the rule, and a trusted read-only tool saves any resource it returns under a fresh generated filename, never one the server's URI chose; left out or `false`, the hint is shown but not used. A skill's own tools entry cannot set it: the key is ignored with a warning. An entry that sets `effect` is not retried in the background when its server is unreachable at startup. A built-in entry that sets `effect` is refused on a save through the Builder or platform.

### Tool selection guidance

| Agent needs to... | Recommended tools |
|-------------------|-------------------|
| Chat with users | `general_agent_tools` + `artifact_management` |
| Process files/documents | `artifact_management` + `general_agent_tools` (for `convert_file_to_markdown`) |
| Fetch web content | `web_tools` |
| Analyze data (CSV, JSON) | `data_analysis` + `artifact_management` |
| Generate/process images | `image_tools` |
| Call external APIs | `web_tools` or MCP tool |
| Access a database | MCP tool (postgres, mysql) or a SQL connector component linked to the agent. Never a `tool_type: builtin` entry named `execute_sql_query` |
| Read or write Excel / Word files | The built-in skill `sam-excel` or `sam-docx` under `skills:`, not a `tool_type: builtin` entry for `xlsx_read` or `docx_create_document` |
| Delegate to other agents | No special tools needed — configure `inter_agent_communication` |

---

## 6. Knowledge-Bundle Skills

Skills are directories containing reference documents that agents can load on demand.

```yaml
skills:
  - name: api-reference                   # Directory name under skills_base_path
  - name: tutorials
```

The platform sets `skills_base_path` and `skills_cache_path`; the Builder does not save them.

**How skills work at runtime:**
1. Agent starts with skills registered but not loaded.
2. Agent calls `load_skill` tool to load a skill's instructions and register its tools.
3. Agent calls `grep_skill_resources` to search reference docs.
4. Agent calls `read_skill_resource` to read specific reference files.

**Instruction integration:** When using skills, include guidance in the instruction:
```
You have access to these skills:
- **api-reference**: API documentation. Load when you need endpoint details.
- **tutorials**: Step-by-step guides. Load when explaining how to do something.

When you need reference material:
1. Load the skill with load_skill
2. Search with grep_skill_resources using broad patterns
3. Read specific sections with read_skill_resource
```

**Decks bring `sam-pptx`.** When the agent can call `pptx_create_presentation` (its tools include
`builtin_document_tools`, or that single tool), saving it adds the built-in skill `sam-pptx` to its
skills. A new agent always gets it. An existing agent gets it only when its artifact lists
`skills:`; otherwise it keeps the skills it has. A listed `skills:` replaces the stored list, so
for an existing agent keep its current skills in the list and add `- name: sam-pptx`. While the
agent has the deck tool, every save that lists `skills:` (even `skills: []`) keeps `sam-pptx`. It covers
planning a deck, gathering the figures inside the call budget, layouts, native charts and a visual
check. Have the instruction load it before building a deck.

## 7. Session Service

Controls conversation memory persistence.

```yaml
session_service:
  type: sql                                        # "memory" or "sql"
  database_url: "sqlite:///${SAM_DATA_DIR}/sam.db"  # SQLite or PostgreSQL
  default_behavior: PERSISTENT                      # PERSISTENT or RUN_BASED
```

| Type | Backend | Use When |
|------|---------|----------|
| `memory` | In-process (lost on restart) | Testing, workflow nodes, stateless agents |
| `sql` + SQLite URL | SQLite file | Single-instance deployments, desktop mode |
| `sql` + PostgreSQL URL | PostgreSQL | Production multi-instance deployments |

**Database URL formats:**
- SQLite: `"sqlite:///path/to/file.db"` or `"sqlite:///${SAM_DATA_DIR}/sam.db"`
- PostgreSQL: `"postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/dbname"`

**Session behavior:**
- `PERSISTENT` — sessions survive restarts, conversation history maintained across sessions
- `RUN_BASED` — sessions scoped to a single agent run, cleared on restart

**Guidance:**
- Interactive chat agents → `sql` with `PERSISTENT` (users expect continuity)
- Autonomous event-driven agents → `memory` (each event is independent)
- Workflow node agents → `memory` (each invocation is stateless)

---

## 8. Artifact Service

Controls where artifacts (files) are stored.

```yaml
artifact_service:
  type: filesystem                              # filesystem | memory | s3 | gcs
  base_path: "${SAM_DATA_DIR}/artifacts"
  artifact_scope: namespace                     # namespace | global
```

| Type | Use When |
|------|----------|
| `filesystem` | Default. Single-instance. Uses local disk. |
| `memory` | Testing only. Lost on restart. |
| `s3` | Production cloud. Requires `bucket_name`, `region`. |
| `gcs` | Google Cloud. Requires `bucket_name`, `credentials_file`. |

**Additional fields for cloud backends:**
```yaml
artifact_service:
  type: s3
  bucket_name: "my-bucket"
  region: "us-east-1"
  endpoint_url: "https://..."      # Optional custom endpoint (MinIO, etc.)
```

**Artifact scope:**
- `namespace` (default) — artifacts are scoped to the agent's namespace
- `global` — artifacts accessible across namespaces

## 9. Artifact Handling Mode

The runtime accepts `ignore`, `embed` or `reference` for this key, but nothing that runs a Builder-saved agent branches on it: files the user attaches reach the agent the same way in every mode.

```yaml
# artifact_handling_mode: ignore    # ignore | embed | reference. Default: ignore
```

The Builder saves this key, but leave it out unless you need a different mode: leaving it out keeps the stored value, and `null` removes it. The agent is told about files the user attaches in any mode; give it `artifact_management` and say in its instruction to `list_artifacts` and `load_artifact` to open them.

**Related settings:**
```yaml
text_artifact_content_max_length: 32768   # Max chars for embedded artifact content
# enable_embed_resolution: true               # Document embeds (math, datetime, status_update) in the prompt. Default: on when the agent has load_artifact
# enable_artifact_content_instruction: true   # Document the artifact_content embed in the prompt. Default: on when the agent has load_artifact
```

### 9.1 An agent can AUTHOR embeds — say so in its instruction

The settings above govern what an agent *reads*. Separately, an agent can **write**
an embed directive into a document or response, and the platform resolves it later:
early embeds (`datetime`, `math`, `uuid`) resolve when the artifact is saved, while
**late embeds (`artifact_content`, `template_liquid`) are preserved verbatim and
resolved by the entrypoint at download time.**

🛑 **This capability is invisible unless the instruction states it, and the failure
is expensive.** An agent asked to assemble a report over images it just produced
will otherwise assume it must inline the bytes — and base64 of even a few PNGs runs
to hundreds of thousands of output tokens. The observed behavior is not an error
message: the agent announces the report, fails to emit it, and the turn ends
"successfully" with no artifact.

**When generating any agent that produces a document referencing artifacts —
reports, summaries with charts, anything with an image — its `instruction` must
include the directive syntax and the prohibition:**

```yaml
instruction: |
  ...
  When your output references an artifact, write an embed directive — never paste
  the artifact's contents or base64 bytes into your response.

    Image:      <img src="«artifact_content:chart.png >>> format:datauri»">
    Text/data:  «artifact_content:results.csv >>> format:csv»

  The directive is resolved when the document is downloaded, so the bytes never
  pass through your output. Valid `format:` values are text, json, json_pretty,
  csv, datauri, and numeric specs like .2f — any other name silently degrades to
  plain text. The target is the artifact's filename.
```

**Prefer a workflow when there is no judgement to apply.** If the document is the
same shape every run, a `.samt` template rendered by an `instantiate_template` tool
node is deterministic and costs zero LLM calls — see `sam-templates` and
`sam-workflow-schema` §2.6. Instruct an agent to author embeds when the report's
*structure* genuinely varies per run.

---

tool_output_llm_return_max_bytes: 4096    # Truncate what the LLM sees to 4KB

Solace Agent Mesh agent configuration schema and practical guide. Every field in an agent's `app_config` is defined below, along with valid values, field interactions, and common patterns.

For **tool details** see `sam-tool-schema`. For **design guidance** see `sam-agent-design`.

## Schema

```yaml
{{SCHEMA:agent}}
```

---

## 1. Identity Fields

Note: System fields (`namespace`, `model`, `display_name`, `session_service`, `artifact_service`, `agent_card_publishing`, `agent_discovery`) are injected by the platform at deployment time and must not be included in generated configs. The one model setting you do write is `model_provider` (section 2).

```yaml
agent_name: my_agent          # Required. Unique ID for broker topics/routing. Use snake_case.
description: "..."             # Required. Free text description of the agent.
version: "1.0"                 # Optional semver string.
agent_type: standard           # "standard" (default) or "workflow" (used by workflow engine).
```

The platform sets `agent_type`; the Builder does not save it.

**Rules:**
- `agent_name` must be unique across the deployment. Convention: `snake_case`, no hyphens.
- For platform-deployed agents, the name is auto-generated as `agent_<uuid>` with underscores.

---

## 2. LLM Model Configuration

### Which model an agent uses: `model_provider`

An agent's model is bound by `model_provider`, a key **inside `app_config`**. It holds the name (the alias on the Models page) of a model the platform has configured:

```yaml
apps:
  - name: my_agent
    app_config:
      agent_name: my_agent
      model_provider: ["planning"]
```

- Get the names from `platform_list_components` with `component_type: model`. Use a chat model; a decision model is refused. A name that is not configured is refused by the save and by the preview.
- Give one entry. The platform binds one model per agent, so a list of two, an empty name, or a value that is not a name is refused.
- Leave `model_provider` out to use the platform default on a new agent. On an existing agent, leaving it out keeps the model the agent already has; `model_provider: []` returns it to the platform default.
- To change the model of an existing agent, edit its artifact and set `app_config.model_provider`. Nothing else changes the model.
- **Never write `model:`**, with a name (`model: general`), a provider string (`model: "openai/gpt-4o"`) or the object form. The platform never reads it, so the agent would stay on its old model. The save and `validate_component_config` refuse it, whether it sits in `app_config` or beside it on the `apps[]` item; so is `model_provider` written beside `app_config` instead of inside it. When the user names a model by its provider string (for example `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`) and no listed name is clearly that model, ask which listed name they mean, or tell them to add one on the Models page: the Builder cannot create models.

### Runtime config files (`sam run`), not the Builder

A hand-written config file that the platform does not generate sets the model with `model:`. Two forms are supported:

#### Simple string form
```yaml
model: "openai/gpt-4o"
```

#### Object form (for custom endpoints)
```yaml
model:
  model: "anthropic/claude-4-5-sonnet"
  api_base: "${LLM_SERVICE_ENDPOINT}"
  api_key: "${LLM_SERVICE_API_KEY}"
  cache_strategy: "5m"         # "none", "5m", "1h" (default "5m")
```

#### Model string format
Format: `"provider/model-name"` — the provider prefix tells the LLM client which API format to use.

**Supported providers and common models:**

| Provider | Example models |
|----------|---------------|
| `openai` | `openai/gpt-4o`, `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, `openai/o3-mini` |
| `anthropic` | `anthropic/claude-4-5-sonnet`, `anthropic/claude-4-5-haiku` |
| `google` | `google/gemini-3.6-flash`, `google/gemini-3.5-flash`, `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` |
| `vertex` | `vertex/gemini-3.5-flash` |
| `bedrock` | `bedrock/anthropic.claude-v2` |
| `azure` | `azure/gpt-4o` (requires api_base pointing to Azure endpoint) |
| `cohere` | `cohere/command-r-plus` |
| `mistral` | `mistral/mistral-large-latest` |
| `groq` | `groq/llama-3.1-70b-versatile` |
| `perplexity` | `perplexity/llama-3.1-sonar-large-128k-online` |
| `ollama` | `ollama/llama3.1` (requires local api_base) |
| `xai` | `xai/grok-2` |
| `openrouter` | `openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.1-405b-instruct` |

**Critical rules:**
- For `openai/` models (which cover any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), `api_base` is either a base URL or the provider's complete chat-completions URL. With a base URL, the client appends `/v1/chat/completions`, dropping one trailing `/v1` from the base first. If the provider does not serve its API under `/v1`, give the complete URL, whose path ends in `/chat/completions` (for example `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/v3/chat/completions`); the client calls it exactly as written. Models that accept a request only through the OpenAI Responses API (the `-pro` models, and some GPT-5 models when the request includes tools) do not work with the complete form.
- In a runtime config file, use env vars: `${LLM_SERVICE_ENDPOINT}`, `${LLM_SERVICE_API_KEY}`, `${LLM_SERVICE_GENERAL_MODEL_NAME}`.

### LLM control parameters
```yaml
supports_streaming: false      # Platform default.
max_tokens: 0                  # 0 = the model's own output ceiling for Claude 5.x on the Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex and Azure providers, otherwise the provider default. Set only if you need to limit output.
# max_llm_calls_per_task: 30   # Model calls per task; 30 is the default. Uncomment and set about 60 only for an agent that gathers data and then builds a document (deck, report).
enable_auto_continuation: true # Allow the agent to continue if response is truncated.
```

The Builder saves every key in this schema. Leaving a key out keeps the agent's stored value; to remove a stored `output_schema`, a setting or a block, write the key with `null`. A value such as `output_schema` is replaced whole, not merged. A key the platform manages (`agent_type`, `internal`, `required_scopes`, `skills_base_path`, `skills_cache_path`, `volumes`, `networks`, and `allow_loopback` inside a built-in tool's `tool_config`) is not saved by the Builder: the save keeps the stored value and warns once if you state one. `null` removes a stored setting with two exceptions: peer access needs `allow_list: []`, and the platform-managed keys cannot be removed from the Builder.

**About `max_llm_calls_per_task`:** a positive whole number is saved with the agent and deployed as written. Zero, a negative number, a fraction or text is refused, and nothing is saved until it is fixed. Leaving the key out of an update keeps the stored limit, and `null` removes it, so the agent runs with the default of 30.

**About `supports_streaming`:** leave it out unless the agent must advertise streaming; a new agent runs with `false`.

## 3. Instruction (System Prompt)

```yaml
instruction: |
  You are a security auditor agent...
```

The instruction is the most important field for agent quality. See the `sam-agent-design` skill for the full five-section writing guide. Key points:

- Use YAML block scalar (`|`) for multi-line instructions.
- Structure: Role → Expertise → Guidelines → Constraints → Skill references.
- Keep under ~2000 tokens. Move reference material into skills.
- For interactive agents: include tone/personality guidance and when to ask for clarification.
- For autonomous agents: explicitly state "do not ask for clarification" and describe fallback behavior.

### Injection flags
```yaml
inject_current_time: true          # Stamps each user turn with weekday, date, time and IANA zone
inject_system_purpose: false       # Prepends Solace Agent Mesh platform purpose statement
inject_response_format: false      # Prepends response format guidance
inject_user_profile: false         # Prepends user profile info (enterprise)
```

These are rarely needed — most agents should set their own context in the instruction.

## 4. Agent Card (Discovery Identity)

**Required for every agent.** Without an agent card, the agent is invisible to entrypoints and peer agents.

```yaml
agent_card:
  description: "Analyzes code for security vulnerabilities and generates compliance reports."
  version: "1.0"
  defaultInputModes: [text]           # What the agent accepts: text, file, data
  defaultOutputModes: [text, file]    # What the agent produces: text, file, data
  skills:                             # Capabilities (NOT knowledge-bundle skills)
    - id: code-review
      name: Code Review
      description: >-
        Review code for security vulnerabilities, performance issues,
        and coding standard violations.
      tags: [security, code-quality]
      examples:
        - "Review this Python file for SQL injection vulnerabilities"
        - "Check this API endpoint for authentication issues"
    - id: compliance-report
      name: Compliance Reporting
      description: >-
        Generate SOC2, PCI-DSS, and HIPAA compliance reports.
  provider:
    organization: "My Company"
    url: "https://example.com"
```

**Important distinctions:**
- `agent_card.skills` = **capabilities** advertised for discovery (A2A protocol term). These are what the entrypoint and peer agents match against when routing tasks.
- `skills` (top-level) = **knowledge-bundle skills** (directories with reference docs). Completely different concept, confusingly similar name.

**Writing good capability descriptions:**
- Each skill.description should be specific enough that the entrypoint can match a user request to it.
- Include keywords the user would naturally use when asking for this capability.
- Keep descriptions non-overlapping across skills on the same agent.
- Bad: `"Does stuff with code."` — Good: `"Reviews Python code for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities with file paths and remediation steps."`

**Input/output modes:**
- `text` — plain text messages (almost always included)
- `file` — file uploads (input) or file artifacts (output)
- `data` — structured data (JSON, CSV, etc.)

## 5. Tool Groups and Individual Tools

### Built-in tool groups

Use `tool_type: builtin-group` to add all tools in a named group:

```yaml
tools:
  - tool_type: builtin-group
    group_name: artifact_management
```

{{TOOL_GROUPS_TABLE}}

### Individual built-in tools

Use `tool_type: builtin` when you need only specific tools or per-tool configuration:

```yaml
tools:
  - tool_type: builtin
    tool_name: web_request
    hil:
      require_approval: true
      approval_message: "This will make an HTTP request."
      timeout: "5m"
      show_args: true
```

### Secure Tool Runtime-backed builtin tools

Tools that ship with Solace Agent Mesh but run out-of-process in the Secure Tool Runtime
(e.g. `mermaid_diagram_generator`, `create_chart_from_plotly_config`,
`execute_python_code`, `ffmpeg`, `pptx_*`) are declared the same way as
in-process builtins when a built-in group registers them. A tool that no built-in group
registers cannot be saved by the Builder under `tool_type: builtin`: a skill's tools
(`xlsx_read`, `docx_create_document`) come with the skill listed under `skills:`, a
connector's runtime (`execute_sql_query`, `graph_db_query`, `slack`) comes with a
connector linked to the agent, and a custom tool ships in an uploaded toolset.

A save that sets `required_scopes` or `auth` on a built-in entry is refused; remove them from the entry.
A save that sets `effect` on a built-in entry is refused as well, because the platform cannot store it and dropping it would loosen the tool's effect classification.

The custom-tool form below is for runtime config files; the Builder does not save it:

```yaml
tools:
  - tool_type: builtin
    tool_name: analyze_data
    tool_description: "Analyzes dataset and produces statistical summary."
    sandbox_profile: standard         # restrictive | standard | permissive
    parameters:
      dataset:
        type: artifact
        description: "The CSV dataset to analyze"
        required: true
      output_format:
        type: string
        description: "Output format: 'summary' or 'detailed'"
        required: false
        default: "summary"
```

**Sandbox profiles:**
- `restrictive` — 512MB RAM, 60s CPU, network isolated. For pure computation.
- `standard` — 1GB RAM, 300s CPU, network access. Default.
- `permissive` — 4GB RAM, 600s CPU, full access. For heavy processing.

**Special parameter types:**
- `artifact` — accepts an artifact filename as input
- `artifact_list` — accepts a list of artifact filenames

### MCP tools (Model Context Protocol)

```yaml
tools:
  - tool_type: mcp
    connection_params:
      type: stdio                      # stdio | sse | streamable-http
      command: "npx"
      args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres"]
      env:
        DATABASE_URL: "${DATABASE_URL}"
    allow_list: [query, list_tables]   # Only expose these tools (optional)
```

**Transport types:**
- `stdio` — local process (command + args). Most common for development.
- `sse` — Server-Sent Events remote server (url required).
- `streamable-http` — HTTP streaming remote server (url required).

**Tool filtering** (mutually exclusive):
- `tool_name` — expose exactly one tool
- `tool_name_prefix` — expose tools matching prefix
- `allow_list` — expose only listed tools
- `deny_list` — expose all except listed tools

**Effect** (optional, per entry): every tool is `read_only` or `side_effecting`, and an MCP tool is `side_effecting` unless told otherwise. A tool is read_only only if all three hold: it cannot change anything outside the run, whatever its input; it fetches no URL chosen by its input or by the content of a file it reads; it writes, deletes or replaces no artifact under a filename chosen by its caller or by the tool itself. The run is the one task that called the tool, and changing something outside it means writing, sending, deleting, posting, publishing or indexing in an external system, another session or user scope, or starting a job. Changing the run's own session, such as the skills it has loaded, is not outside it. A filename is chosen by the caller when it comes from a parameter, and by the tool when its code fixes or derives it, including a name set on a data object it returns. A result the runtime itself saves under a fresh filename it picks, which it does only when a tool returns data with no name set (auto-disposition), is not a write. Sending the caller's query to one fixed external service, as a search or lookup does, is not fetching a chosen URL. Every other tool is side_effecting. `effect: side_effecting` marks every tool the entry registers side-effecting; `read_only` is not accepted. `trust_annotations: true` lets the server's own `readOnlyHint: true` make its tools `read_only` only when the server also sends `openWorldHint: false` (an omitted `openWorldHint` counts as `true`, the MCP default) and no `destructiveHint: true`; you vouch that such tools meet all three conditions of the rule, and a trusted read-only tool saves any resource it returns under a fresh generated filename, never one the server's URI chose; left out or `false`, the hint is shown but not used. A skill's own tools entry cannot set it: the key is ignored with a warning. An entry that sets `effect` is not retried in the background when its server is unreachable at startup. A built-in entry that sets `effect` is refused on a save through the Builder or platform.

### Tool selection guidance

| Agent needs to... | Recommended tools |
|-------------------|-------------------|
| Chat with users | `general_agent_tools` + `artifact_management` |
| Process files/documents | `artifact_management` + `general_agent_tools` (for `convert_file_to_markdown`) |
| Fetch web content | `web_tools` |
| Analyze data (CSV, JSON) | `data_analysis` + `artifact_management` |
| Generate/process images | `image_tools` |
| Call external APIs | `web_tools` or MCP tool |
| Access a database | MCP tool (postgres, mysql) or a SQL connector component linked to the agent. Never a `tool_type: builtin` entry named `execute_sql_query` |
| Read or write Excel / Word files | The built-in skill `sam-excel` or `sam-docx` under `skills:`, not a `tool_type: builtin` entry for `xlsx_read` or `docx_create_document` |
| Delegate to other agents | No special tools needed — configure `inter_agent_communication` |

## 6. Knowledge-Bundle Skills

Skills are directories containing reference documents that agents can load on demand.

```yaml
skills:
  - name: api-reference                   # Directory name under skills_base_path
  - name: tutorials
```

The platform sets `skills_base_path` and `skills_cache_path`; the Builder does not save them.

**How skills work at runtime:**
1. Agent starts with skills registered but not loaded.
2. Agent calls `load_skill` tool to load a skill's instructions and register its tools.
3. Agent calls `grep_skill_resources` to search reference docs.
4. Agent calls `read_skill_resource` to read specific reference files.

**Instruction integration:** When using skills, include guidance in the instruction:
```
You have access to these skills:
- **api-reference**: API documentation. Load when you need endpoint details.
- **tutorials**: Step-by-step guides. Load when explaining how to do something.

When you need reference material:
1. Load the skill with load_skill
2. Search with grep_skill_resources using broad patterns
3. Read specific sections with read_skill_resource
```

---
name: sam-connector-design
description: Design guidance for Solace Agent Mesh connectors — when to use each type, how they relate to agents, builder workflow, and secret handling.
---

Design guidance for creating Solace Agent Mesh connectors. Connectors are reusable credential + tool bundles that get linked to agents.

For **schema details** see `sam-connector-schema`.

## What Are Connectors?

Connectors provide agents with access to external systems. The list below
illustrates the native connector types; it is not the catalogue of this
deployment. A type can be switched off (the `email` type is off unless the
deployment enables it). Call `platform_list_components` with
`component_type: connector_type` to get the types and subtypes this deployment has
enabled, and never propose a connector type it does not list. When a need
points at a type that is not listed, say which capability is off and what would
enable it; do not substitute an invented tool. `sam-connector-schema` holds the
field schema of each type:
- **SQL** (`sql`): Query databases — PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MSSQL, Oracle
- **MCP** (`mcp`): Connect to remote MCP tool servers (GitHub, Stripe, custom servers)
- **API** (`api`): Call REST APIs via OpenAPI specifications
- **Knowledge Base** (`knowledge_base`): RAG retrieval from Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
- **Slack** (`slack`): Post/read messages in a Slack workspace via a Slack bot token (subtype `bot`)
- **Search** (`search`): Full-text search over Elasticsearch or OpenSearch
- **Document DB** (`document_db`): NoSQL document stores — MongoDB, DynamoDB
- **Graph DB** (`graph_db`): Graph databases — Neo4j, Neptune
- **Event Mesh** (`event_mesh`): Publish or request-reply through a Solace event broker from an agent-callable tool
- **Web Search** (`web_search`): Search the public web through Tavily (subtype `tavily`) or Exa (subtype `exa`) and cite the results

Slack, Search, Document DB, Graph DB, and Web Search are FIRST-CLASS connector types —
create them directly (e.g. a Slack request → a `slack` connector), NOT an MCP or
API connector. Reach for MCP only when the user names an MCP/tool server, and for
API only when the user has an OpenAPI/REST spec with no native connector for it.

Connectors are **shared resources** — one connector can be linked to multiple agents (up to 5 agents per connector). This avoids duplicating credentials.

## When to Use Each Type

**SQL** — User mentions:
- Databases, queries, SQL, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB
- "I want the agent to query our database"
- "Connect to our data warehouse"

**MCP** — User mentions:
- MCP servers, tool servers, remote tools
- Specific MCP servers (GitHub, Stripe, custom MCP servers)
- "Connect to an MCP server"
- SSE or streamable-http connections

**Knowledge Base** — User mentions:
- RAG, knowledge bases, document search
- Amazon Bedrock, AWS knowledge base
- "Search through our documentation"

**API** — User mentions:
- REST APIs, OpenAPI, Swagger
- "Call an external API"
- Specific API services with OpenAPI specs

**Slack** — User mentions:
- Slack, a Slack workspace/channel, a Slack bot, posting or reading Slack messages
- "Create a Slack connector", "connect to Slack", a Slack bot token / app token
- Use a native `slack` connector (subtype `bot`) — do NOT route this to MCP or API

**Search** — User mentions:
- Full-text search, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch
- "Search our Elasticsearch index"

**Web Search** — User mentions:
- Searching the internet or the public web, current events, citing web sources
- Tavily or Exa, or "give the agent web search"
- Use a `web_search` connector with the provider the user names, and
  `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` for `api_key`. Leave `api_base` out: the connector
  supplies the provider's endpoint. When no provider is named, ask which one
  the user has a key for. `search` is the Elasticsearch / OpenSearch type, not web search.
  Its tool is for agent nodes; a workflow tool node cannot use it.

**Document DB** — User mentions:
- MongoDB, DynamoDB, a NoSQL/document store
- "Query our MongoDB collection"

**Graph DB** — User mentions:
- Neo4j, Neptune, a graph database, relationships/traversals
- "Query our knowledge graph"

**Event Mesh** — User mentions:
- Solace event broker, event mesh connector, broker-backed tools
- "Publish to a topic from an agent"
- "Send a command through the event broker"
- "Use request-reply over Solace"
- "Connect the agent to a backend service through the event broker"

Use an **Event Mesh Connector** when the agent initiates the interaction by invoking a tool. Use an **Event Mesh Entrypoint** instead when an external broker event arrives first and should autonomously trigger an agent or workflow.

For Event Mesh Connectors, do not infer an input schema from topic names. Ask for Topic Address plus the real operation schema. Once the user provides both, infer low-risk configuration rather than asking a long checklist:
- derive tool name and description from topic, schema, and use case
- match Topic Address variables to schema properties
- use existing `x-solace-payload-path`; otherwise map payload properties to their own names and leave topic-only variables out of payload
- default payload format to JSON
- default Delivery Mode to Guaranteed Messaging
- infer Publish-Subscribe for command/event topics; infer Request-Reply for query/get/check/status topics or when the user needs a backend result
- default Request-Reply to `reply_mode: temp_queue` and `request_expiry_ms: 60000`

Ask follow-up questions only when the inference is ambiguous or high impact. If the user provides only topic addresses, ask them to paste or describe the input schema and payload mappings, or explicitly confirm they will configure schemas later in the connector UI.

After a schema is provided, review every property that the agent can supply. If an ambiguous property lacks a `description`, ask the user for one and add it to the JSON Schema. Ambiguous examples include IDs, codes, action/status fields, quantities, units, dates, free-text notes, business abbreviations, and conditionally required inputs. Do not invent these descriptions unless the user or source schema already supplied the meaning.

When asking for human-authored wording such as tool names, tool descriptions, operation descriptions, or missing schema-property descriptions, offer 2-4 AI-generated options where possible and let the user choose or write their own. Do not use generated options for exact system values such as credentials, URLs, topic addresses, IDs, or pasted schemas.

## Builder Workflow for Connectors

### 1. Identify connector needs during Discovery phase

When the user describes what they want the agent to do, listen for signals that suggest connectors:
- External data sources → SQL, Document DB, Graph DB, Search, or Knowledge Base
- Slack workspace/bot → Slack
- External tool servers → MCP
- External APIs → API (OpenAPI)
- Agent-initiated Solace publish or request-reply flows → Event Mesh

Check each candidate against the enabled types (see "What Are Connectors?"), and don't substitute a tool or built-in that `describe_tools` doesn't show.

### 2. Create connector artifacts BEFORE agent artifacts

Connectors should be created before agents because agents reference connectors. The build manifest should list connectors first.

### 3. Gather information conversationally

Ask about the system, not the credentials:
- "What database system are you using?" (not "What's the password?")
- "Does the MCP server require authentication?" (not "What's the API key?")
- "What region is your knowledge base in?"
- "What is the URL of the API's OpenAPI (Swagger) document?" (an API connector built here needs it; if they only have a file, they create the connector on the Connectors page and the build reuses it)
- "For each Event Mesh operation, can you paste the JSON Schema or Event Portal/AsyncAPI schema and identify which fields go into the Topic Address versus the payload?"
- "Should this Event Mesh operation use Publish-Subscribe or Request-Reply? If Request-Reply, what reply delivery and timeout should it use?"
- "Which Delivery Mode should the outbound message use: Guaranteed Messaging or Direct Messaging?"
- "These schema fields are missing descriptions: action, sku, quantity. What should the agent know about each one?"
- "Which generated tool description best matches this operation? You can choose one or write your own."

Fill in what you learn from conversation and use `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` for everything else, especially secrets.

### 4. Use discovery tools when possible

- **MCP connectors**: If the user provides a server URL and no auth is needed (or they've provided credentials), use `discover_mcp_tools` to list available tools and their parameters. This helps write a better connector description, and it gives the parameter names a workflow tool node needs.
- **API connectors**: Use `parse_openapi_spec` to detect what authentication the API requires (this sets the correct `auth_type`) and to list the API's operations and their parameters, as `toolName: in(param*, ...)` in the preview and in full in `openapi_spec.json`. A workflow tool node needs an `allow_list` or an uploaded spec; a connector created from only a spec URL needs the operation's `operationId` in its `allow_list`, because a `toolName` is the operationId snake-cased and cut to 60 characters; when the preview shows `toolName [operationId: X]`, write `X`. With a long operation list, pass `operations: [names]` to read specific ones. If the preview says `operations: could not be read (<reason>)`, don't guess operations: use an agent node, or ask the user to upload a bundled single-file spec on the Connectors page.
- **Connectors already on the platform**: use `describe_tools` with `{connector: <exact name>}` to see their tools' parameters (up to 50 are listed; add `tool` to describe one by name).

If discovery isn't possible (auth required but not provided), skip it — the UI handles discovery after credentials are filled in.

### 5. Validate before saving

Always validate connector artifacts with `validate_component_config`:
```
validate_component_config(
  config_yaml: '<the JSON string>',
  mime_type: 'application/vnd.sam-connector-config+json'
)
```

Note: despite the parameter name `config_yaml`, pass JSON for connectors.

## Secret Handling

**Never include real secrets in artifacts.** Always use `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>`:
- Passwords, API keys, tokens, secret keys
- Any credential the user hasn't explicitly provided in chat

The UI detects `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` and blocks build and test until it is replaced. No dialog collects it: the user tells you the value and you rewrite the artifact, or they edit the connector on the Connectors page once it is saved.

It's fine to include non-secret values the user mentions:
- Hostnames, ports, database names
- URLs, regions, connection types
- Auth types (API connectors: none/apikey/http/oauth)

**Validate a credential the user DID provide before proceeding.** When the user
supplies a concrete secret value in chat (e.g. a Slack bot token), put it in the
config and then re-run `validate_component_config` on that concrete config — do NOT
validate only the `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>` placeholder and then swap the value in
unchecked. If validation fails on the provided value (e.g. "Bot Token must start
with 'xoxb-'", or a minimum-length error), do NOT stamp the component validated
or claim it's deployed. Instead tell the user in prose exactly what's wrong and ask
them to give you the corrected value in the chat, then write it into the artifact with
`artifact_search_and_replace_regex`. Never ask for a secret through `ask_user_question`
— that field is not masked. (Or offer to save with the `<<__SAM_REQUIRED__>>`
placeholder, which they can replace later by telling you or, once the connector is
saved, on the Connectors page.) A
malformed credential will be rejected by the platform at save time, so proceeding
only produces a confusing failure.

## Connector-Agent Relationship

- Each agent can have up to 5 connectors
- Each connector generates tool entries in the agent's YAML, and the shape depends on the
  connector type:
  - SQL, Slack, Search, Document DB, Graph DB, Knowledge Base and Event Mesh
    connectors emit `tool_type: builtin` entries with a generated per-connector
    `tool_name`, each backed by a shared runtime binary (a SQL connector's tool runs on
    `execute_sql_query`, a Slack connector's on `slack` and `slack_update`).
  - An **MCP** connector emits a single `tool_type: mcp` entry carrying connection
    params. Its tool names usually come from the remote MCP server at connect time,
    so they are not knowable from the YAML. A `manifest` or a `tool_name` on the entry
    does pin them — the manifest IS the registered tool set, and `tool_name` narrows to
    that one tool. A `tool_name_prefix` does not: the names stay whatever the server
    advertises, each carrying that prefix.
  - An **API** connector emits a `tool_type: openapi` entry pointing at the spec; its
    tool names come from the OpenAPI operations.

  Read the generated YAML rather than guessing a connector tool's name.
- Connectors are referenced by ID in the agent record
- The platform handles linking connectors to agents — the builder just creates the connector artifact and lists it in the build manifest
- Approval gates for connector tools live on the connector (`values.hil`), see
  `sam-connector-schema` → Tool Approvals. Tell the user they apply to every agent using
  the connector, and that workflow tool nodes bound to it run without asking, so a tool
  that needs approval goes through an agent node. Keys are role names (`sql_query`,
  `slack_send_message`), and
  `api` keys are the snake_case operation tool name. Writing `hil` replaces the whole
  block; `"hil": {}` or `null` removes it in a build. Deselecting an `api` operation keeps
  its gate, but uploading a spec that drops it, or renaming or removing an `event_mesh`
  operation, removes that gate with a warning that the save reports. To keep a gate on a
  renamed `event_mesh` operation, write the new `hil` in the same build.

## Build Manifest

Include connectors in the build manifest with their type and subtype:

```yaml
components:
  - filename: my_database.json
    type: connector
    name: my_database
    description: PostgreSQL connector for the analytics database.
    connector_type: sql
    connector_subtype: postgres
  - filename: my_agent.yaml
    type: agent
    name: my_agent
    description: Answers questions against the analytics database.
    connectors:
      - my_database
```

`filename` names the saved artifact and is required on every component — write
`filename: ""` for one that is already running rather than omitting the key.
