skills.name: sam-skill-schema
skills.desc: YAML Schema for Solace Agent Mesh skill configuration — all fields, types, validation rules, reference model, and complete examples.
skills.body:
---
name: sam-skill-schema
description: YAML Schema for Solace Agent Mesh skill configuration — all fields, types, validation rules, reference model, and complete examples.
tags:
  - builder
  - schema
  - skill
  - sam
---

Solace Agent Mesh skill configuration schema. Skills are knowledge bundles with instruction content and optional reference documents that agents load on demand.

For **design guidance** see `sam-skill-design`.

## Schema

```yaml
{{SCHEMA:skill}}
```

---

## Skill Config Format

Skill artifacts use **YAML** with a flat top-level structure (NOT `apps[].app_config`):

```yaml
name: my-api-reference
description: "REST API reference documentation for the Acme platform."
tags:
  - api
  - documentation
examples:
  - "How do I authenticate with the API?"
  - "What endpoints are available?"
instruction_content: |
  # Acme API Reference
  This skill provides documentation for the Acme REST API.
  Use grep_skill_resources to search for endpoints.
references:
  - name: endpoints.md
    content: |
      # Endpoints
      ## GET /users
      Returns a list of users.
  - name: full_spec.md
    artifact: uploaded_openapi_spec
```

**MIME type**: `application/vnd.sam-skill-config+yaml`

---

## Field Reference

### Required Fields

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|-------------|
| `name` | string | 2-60 chars, pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` | Skill identifier. Lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens. |
| `description` | string | 10-500 chars | What this skill provides. Shown for discovery. |
| `instruction_content` | string | 50-50000 chars | Markdown instruction body. Injected into agent context on `load_skill`. |

### Optional Fields

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|-------------|
| `tags` | array of strings | max 20 items | Categorization tags for discovery and filtering. |
| `examples` | array of strings | max 10 items | Example user queries. Used by entrypoint for routing. |
| `required_scopes` | array of strings | — | **Deprecated, ignored** — skill loading is not scope-gated. |
| `tools` | array of objects | — | Tools attached when this skill is loaded. Entries mirror an agent's `tools:` block, e.g. `- tool_type: builtin` / `tool_name: <name>`. |
| `required_builtins` | array of strings | — | **Deprecated** — use `tools:` with `tool_type: builtin` instead. Built-in tool names needed when this skill is loaded. |
| `references` | array of objects | — | Reference documents (see Reference Model below). |
| `assets` | array of objects | — | Binary or opaque files packaged under `assets/` (see Asset Model below). |

---

## Reference Model

Each reference entry has a `name` and exactly one of `content` or `artifact`:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | string | yes | Filename in the references/ directory (e.g., `api_reference.md`). |
| `content` | string | one of content/artifact | Inline reference content. |
| `artifact` | string | one of content/artifact | Artifact name containing the reference content. |

**Rules:**
- Each reference **must** have exactly one of `content` or `artifact` — not both, not neither
- `content` is for builder-generated references (inline in the config)
- `artifact` is for documents in the current session's artifact store — user uploads or tool outputs — referenced by artifact name
- No additional properties allowed on reference entries

---

## Asset Model

Assets are files packaged into the skill bundle's `assets/` directory. Unlike references they may be **binary** (e.g. a packaged `.samt` report template), so there is no inline `content` variant — each entry pulls a session artifact into the bundle:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | string | yes | Filename in the assets/ directory (e.g., `quarterly_report.samt`). |
| `artifact` | string | yes | Session artifact whose bytes are packaged as `assets/<name>`. |

**Rules:**
- `artifact` is required — assets are artifact-only, never inline
- The named artifact must exist in the current session (uploaded by the user or produced by a tool such as `package_template`); the save fails otherwise
- No additional properties allowed on asset entries

---

## Validation Rules

- `name` must match pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` — no uppercase, no underscores, no spaces
- `description` must be 10-500 characters
- `instruction_content` must be 50-50000 characters
- Each reference must have exactly one of `content` or `artifact`
- Each asset must have both `name` and `artifact` (no inline content variant)
- No additional top-level properties allowed (`additionalProperties: false`)
- No additional properties on reference or asset entries (`additionalProperties: false`)

---

## Complete Examples

### Minimal Skill

```yaml
name: coding-standards
description: "Coding standards and style guide for the engineering team."
instruction_content: |
  # Coding Standards

  This skill provides the team's coding standards. Reference it when
  reviewing code or generating new code.

  ## Key Principles
  - Use descriptive variable names
  - Keep functions under 50 lines
  - Write tests for all public functions
  - Use meaningful commit messages
```

### Skill with Inline References

```yaml
name: api-reference
description: "REST API documentation with endpoint details and examples."
tags:
  - api
  - documentation
examples:
  - "How do I call the users endpoint?"
  - "What authentication does the API use?"
instruction_content: |
  # API Reference Skill

  This skill contains documentation for the Acme REST API v2.

  ## Available References
  - `endpoints.md` — Complete endpoint listing
  - `examples.md` — Request/response examples

  When you need endpoint details:
  1. Search with grep_skill_resources for the endpoint or method
  2. Read the relevant section with read_skill_resource
references:
  - name: endpoints.md
    content: |
      # API Endpoints

      ## Authentication
      All endpoints require Bearer token in the Authorization header.

      ## GET /api/v2/users
      Returns a paginated list of users.

      Parameters:
      - page (integer, optional): Page number, default 1
      - limit (integer, optional): Items per page, default 20

      ## POST /api/v2/users
      Creates a new user.

      Body:
      - name (string, required): User display name
      - email (string, required): User email address
  - name: examples.md
    content: |
      # API Examples

      ## List users
      ```
      GET /api/v2/users?page=1&limit=10
      Authorization: Bearer <token>
      ```

      ## Create user
      ```
      POST /api/v2/users
      Authorization: Bearer <token>
      Content-Type: application/json

      {"name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@example.com"}
      ```
```

### Skill with Artifact References

```yaml
name: product-docs
description: "Product documentation uploaded by the team."
tags:
  - product
  - documentation
instruction_content: |
  # Product Documentation

  This skill contains the team's product documentation.
  Use grep_skill_resources to search across all documents.

  ## Available Documents
  - `user_guide.md` — End-user documentation
  - `admin_guide.md` — Administrator documentation
references:
  - name: user_guide.md
    artifact: uploaded_user_guide
  - name: admin_guide.md
    artifact: uploaded_admin_guide
```

### Skill with a Binary Asset

```yaml
name: quarterly-report
description: "Renders the quarterly business report from a packaged template."
tags:
  - reporting
instruction_content: |
  # Quarterly Report Skill

  This skill ships a packaged report template (`quarterly_report.samt`)
  produced by the package_template tool.

  To render the report, call instantiate_template with:
  - skill_name: quarterly-report
  - asset: quarterly_report.samt
  - the data fields the template declares
assets:
  - name: quarterly_report.samt
    artifact: packaged_quarterly_report
```

### Skill with Mixed References

```yaml
name: compliance-rules
description: "Compliance rules and regulatory requirements for data handling."
tags:
  - compliance
  - security
  - regulations
examples:
  - "What are the data retention requirements?"
  - "How should PII be handled?"
instruction_content: |
  # Compliance Rules

  This skill provides compliance and regulatory guidance.

  ## Quick Reference
  - PII must be encrypted at rest and in transit
  - Data retention: 7 years for financial, 3 years for operational
  - Access logs must be maintained for all PII access

  ## Detailed References
  - `overview.md` — Summary of compliance requirements (generated)
  - `full_policy.md` — Complete compliance policy document (uploaded)

  Search references with grep_skill_resources for specific regulations.
references:
  - name: overview.md
    content: |
      # Compliance Overview

      ## Data Classification
      - Public: No restrictions
      - Internal: Access controls required
      - Confidential: Encryption + access logs
      - Restricted: All of the above + approval workflow

      ## Key Regulations
      - GDPR: EU data protection
      - SOC2: Security controls
      - PCI-DSS: Payment card data
  - name: full_policy.md
    artifact: uploaded_compliance_policy
```

---

## Build Manifest Entry

Skills appear in the build manifest as `type: skill`:

```yaml
components:
  - filename: api_reference.yaml
    type: skill
    name: api-reference
    description: "REST API reference documentation."
    status: validated
    origin: session
  - filename: my_agent.yaml
    type: agent
    name: MyAgent
    description: "Agent that uses the API reference skill."
    status: validated
    origin: session
    depends_on: []
    skills: [api-reference]
```

Agents reference skills by name in the manifest's `skills` array. This is validated during full manifest validation (`full_validation=true`).

```yaml
tags:
  - api
  - documentation
examples:
  - "How do I authenticate with the API?"
  - "What endpoints are available?"
instruction_content: |
  # Acme API Reference
  This skill provides documentation for the Acme REST API.
  Use grep_skill_resources to search for endpoints.
references:
  - name: endpoints.md
    content: |
      # Endpoints
      ## GET /users
      Returns a list of users.
  - name: full_spec.md
    artifact: uploaded_openapi_spec
```

**MIME type**: `application/vnd.sam-skill-config+yaml`

---

## Field Reference

### Required Fields

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|-------------|
| `name` | string | 2-60 chars, pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` | Skill identifier. Lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens. |
| `description` | string | 10-500 chars | What this skill provides. Shown for discovery. |
| `instruction_content` | string | 50-50000 chars | Markdown instruction body. Injected into agent context on `load_skill`. |

### Optional Fields

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|-------------|
| `tags` | array of strings | max 20 items | Categorization tags for discovery and filtering. |
| `examples` | array of strings | max 10 items | Example user queries. Used by entrypoint for routing. |
| `required_scopes` | array of strings | — | **Deprecated, ignored** — skill loading is not scope-gated. |
| `tools` | array of objects | — | Tools attached when this skill is loaded. Entries mirror an agent's `tools:` block, e.g. `- tool_type: builtin` / `tool_name: <name>`. |
| `required_builtins` | array of strings | — | **Deprecated** — use `tools:` with `tool_type: builtin` instead. Built-in tool names needed when this skill is loaded. |
| `references` | array of objects | — | Reference documents (see Reference Model below). |
| `assets` | array of objects | — | Binary or opaque files packaged under `assets/` (see Asset Model below). |

---

## Reference Model

Each reference entry has a `name` and exactly one of `content` or `artifact`:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | string | yes | Filename in the references/ directory (e.g., `api_reference.md`). |
| `content` | string | one of content/artifact | Inline reference content. |
| `artifact` | string | one of content/artifact | Artifact name containing the reference content. |

**Rules:**
- Each reference **must** have exactly one of `content` or `artifact` — not both, not neither
- `content` is for builder-generated references (inline in the config)
- `artifact` is for documents in the current session's artifact store — user uploads or tool outputs — referenced by artifact name
- No additional properties allowed on reference entries

---

## Asset Model

Assets are files packaged into the skill bundle's `assets/` directory. Unlike references they may be **binary** (e.g. a packaged `.samt` report template), so there is no inline `content` variant — each entry pulls a session artifact into the bundle:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | string | yes | Filename in the assets/ directory (e.g., `quarterly_report.samt`). |
| `artifact` | string | yes | Session artifact whose bytes are packaged as `assets/<name>`. |

**Rules:**
- `artifact` is required — assets are artifact-only, never inline
- The named artifact must exist in the current session (uploaded by the user or produced by a tool such as `package_template`); the save fails otherwise
- No additional properties allowed on asset entries

---

## Validation Rules

- `name` must match pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` — no uppercase, no underscores, no spaces
- `description` must be 10-500 characters
- `instruction_content` must be 50-50000 characters
- Each reference must have exactly one of `content` or `artifact`
- Each asset must have both `name` and `artifact` (no inline content variant)
- No additional top-level properties allowed (`additionalProperties: false`)
- No additional properties on reference or asset entries (`additionalProperties: false`)

---

## Complete Examples

### Minimal Skill

```yaml
name: coding-standards
description: "Coding standards and style guide for the engineering team."
instruction_content: |
  # Coding Standards

  This skill provides the team's coding standards. Reference it when
  reviewing code or generating new code.

  ## Key Principles
  - Use descriptive variable names
  - Keep functions under 50 lines
  - Write tests for all public functions
  - Use meaningful commit messages
```

### Skill with Inline References

```yaml
name: api-reference
description: "REST API documentation with endpoint details and examples."
tags:
  - api
  - documentation
examples:
  - "How do I call the users endpoint?"
  - "What authentication does the API use?"
instruction_content: |
  # API Reference Skill

  This skill contains documentation for the Acme REST API v2.

  ## Available References
  - `endpoints.md` — Complete endpoint listing
  - `examples.md` — Request/response examples

  When you need endpoint details:
  1. Search with grep_skill_resources for the endpoint or method
  2. Read the relevant section with read_skill_resource
references:
  - name: endpoints.md
    content: |
      # API Endpoints

      ## Authentication
      All endpoints require Bearer token in the Authorization header.

      ## GET /api/v2/users
      Returns a paginated list of users.

      Parameters:
      - page (integer, optional): Page number, default 1
      - limit (integer, optional): Items per page, default 20

      ## POST /api/v2/users
      Creates a new user.

      Body:
      - name (string, required): User display name
      - email (string, required): User email address
  - name: examples.md
    content: |
      # API Examples

      ## List users
      ```
      GET /api/v2/users?page=1&limit=10
      Authorization: Bearer <token>
      ```

      ## Create user
      ```
      POST /api/v2/users
      Authorization: Bearer <token>
      Content-Type: application/json

      {"name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@example.com"}
      ```
```

### Skill with Artifact References

```yaml
name: product-docs
description: "Product documentation uploaded by the team."
tags:
  - product
  - documentation
instruction_content: |
  # Product Documentation

  This skill contains the team's product documentation.
  Use grep_skill_resources to search across all documents.

  ## Available Documents
  - `user_guide.md` — End-user documentation
  - `admin_guide.md` — Administrator documentation
references:
  - name: user_guide.md
    artifact: uploaded_user_guide
  - name: admin_guide.md
    artifact: uploaded_admin_guide
```

### Skill with a Binary Asset

```yaml
name: quarterly-report
description: "Renders the quarterly business report from a packaged template."
tags:
  - reporting
instruction_content: |
  # Quarterly Report Skill

  This skill ships a packaged report template (`quarterly_report.samt`)
  produced by the package_template tool.

  To render the report, call instantiate_template with:
  - skill_name: quarterly-report
  - asset: quarterly_report.samt
  - the data fields the template declares
assets:
  - name: quarterly_report.samt
    artifact: packaged_quarterly_report
```

### Skill with Mixed References

```yaml
name: compliance-rules
description: "Compliance rules and regulatory requirements for data handling."
tags:
  - compliance
  - security
  - regulations
examples:
  - "What are the data retention requirements?"
  - "How should PII be handled?"
instruction_content: |
  # Compliance Rules

  This skill provides compliance and regulatory guidance.

  ## Quick Reference
  - PII must be encrypted at rest and in transit
  - Data retention: 7 years for financial, 3 years for operational
  - Access logs must be maintained for all PII access

  ## Detailed References
  - `overview.md` — Summary of compliance requirements (generated)
  - `full_policy.md` — Complete compliance policy document (uploaded)

  Search references with grep_skill_resources for specific regulations.
references:
  - name: overview.md
    content: |
      # Compliance Overview

      ## Data Classification
      - Public: No restrictions
      - Internal: Access controls required
      - Confidential: Encryption + access logs
      - Restricted: All of the above + approval workflow

      ## Key Regulations
      - GDPR: EU data protection
      - SOC2: Security controls
      - PCI-DSS: Payment card data
  - name: full_policy.md
    artifact: uploaded_compliance_policy
```

---

## Build Manifest Entry

Skills appear in the build manifest as `type: skill`:

```yaml
components:
  - filename: api_reference.yaml
    type: skill
    name: api-reference
    description: "REST API reference documentation."
    status: validated
    origin: session
  - filename: my_agent.yaml
    type: agent
    name: MyAgent
    description: "Agent that uses the API reference skill."
    status: validated
    origin: session
    depends_on: []
    skills: [api-reference]
```

Agents reference skills by name in the manifest's `skills` array. This is validated during full manifest validation (`full_validation=true`).

Solace Agent Mesh tool configuration schema. Defines every tool type in an agent's `tools[]` array.

For **agent-level config** see `sam-agent-schema`. For **design guidance** see `sam-best-practices`.

## Schema

```yaml
{{SCHEMA:tool}}
```

## Secure Tool Runtime Manifest (separate from agent config)

```yaml
# tools/manifest.yaml — defines Python tools for the Secure Tool Runtime
version: 1
tools:
  my_tool:
    module: "my_package.my_module"
    function: "my_tool_function"
    package: "my-package"
    version: ">=1.0,<2.0"
    sandbox_profile: "standard"
    timeout_seconds: 30
```

## Examples

Mixed tool types:
```yaml
tools:
  - tool_type: builtin-group
    group_name: artifact_management
  - tool_type: builtin
    tool_name: web_request
    hil: { require_approval: true, timeout: "5m" }
  - tool_type: mcp
    connection_params:
      type: stdio
      command: "npx"
      args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres"]
      env: { DATABASE_URL: "${DATABASE_URL}" }
    allow_list: [query, list_tables]
  - tool_type: builtin
    tool_name: mermaid_diagram_generator   # resolves via the Secure Tool Runtime at runtime
```

skills.name: sam-workflow-schema
skills.desc: JSON Schema for Solace Agent Mesh workflow configuration — node types, templates, conditions, retry, timeouts, exit handlers, and examples.
skills.body:
---
name: sam-workflow-schema
description: JSON Schema for Solace Agent Mesh workflow configuration — node types, templates, conditions, retry, timeouts, exit handlers, and examples.
---

Solace Agent Mesh workflow configuration schema and practical guide. Workflows are DAGs of nodes with deterministic control flow. They publish an agent card and look like any other agent to the system.

For **design guidance** see `sam-workflow-design`. For **agent config** within nodes see `sam-agent-schema`.

## Schema

```yaml
{{SCHEMA:workflow}}
```

---

## 1. Workflow Identity and Required Fields

> **Note:** System fields like `namespace`, `session_service`, and `artifact_service` are injected by the platform at deployment time and must not be included in generated configs.

```yaml
apps:
  - name: my_workflow
    app_config:
      agent_name: my_workflow          # Required. Unique identifier.
      agent_type: workflow             # Required. Must be "workflow".
      description: "..."              # Optional.
      version: "1.0"                  # Optional.
      nodes: [...]                    # Required. At least one node.
      output_mapping: {...}           # Required. Maps workflow output.
```

**Rules:**
- `agent_type: workflow` is required — this is what distinguishes a workflow from an agent.
- `agent_name` must be unique across the deployment, same as agents. Convention: `snake_case`.
- `nodes` and `output_mapping` are both required — a workflow must have at least one node and must define how its output is constructed.

---

## 2. Node Types

Every node has `id` (unique within the workflow) and `type`. Different types require different fields.

### 2.1 Agent Node

Invokes a deployed agent. The most common node type.

```yaml
- id: analyze
  type: agent
  agent_name: Analyzer              # Required. Must match a deployed agent.
  depends_on: [extract]             # Nodes that must complete first.
  input:                            # Data passed to the agent. Values can be templates.
    data: "{{extract.output.text}}" # `extract` declares `text` and `has_data` in its output schema (its agent's
                                    # `output_schema` or an `output_schema_override` on the `extract` node).
  instruction: "Focus on security issues only."  # Optional. Appended to agent's instruction.
  timeout: "2m"                     # Optional. Overrides default_node_timeout.
  when: "'{{extract.output.has_data}}' == 'true'"  # Optional. Skip if false. `has_data` is declared by `extract`.
  retry_strategy:                   # Optional. Overrides workflow-level retry.
    limit: 2
    retry_policy: OnError
  input_schema_override: {...}      # Optional. Override agent's input_schema for this invocation.
  output_schema_override: {...}     # Optional. Override agent's output_schema for this invocation.
```

**Agent node requirements:**
- The agent referenced by `agent_name` must be deployed separately as its own agent config.
- Workflow node agents should use `supports_streaming: false` and define `output_schema` so the workflow can reliably consume structured output.
- 🛑 **Reference `{{<id>.output.<field>}}` only for a field the node declares** — in its `output_schema_override` or its agent's `output_schema` — and make the agent's `instruction` (or the node's `instruction`) tell it to return exactly those keys. An agent node that declares no output schema guarantees no fields: its output is whatever structured result the agent returned, else `{"text": "..."}` — so not even `text` is guaranteed: an agent that returns a structured result has no `text`. When the shape is not declared, bind the whole `{{<id>.output}}` in `output_mapping` or a node `input:`; a switch case or a map node's `items` needs a field, so declare it. To add a field to a node that already has a schema, extend that schema — a new `output_schema_override` replaces the agent's whole schema. This applies to `output_mapping`, node `input:`, `when:`, switch/loop conditions and the `<route_on>` field a rerouting decision node reads from its escalate target alike. Build validation (`validate_build_manifest` with `full_validation: true`) rejects a field reference into an agent node in the build that declares no output schema, and a field outside the schema it does declare (`properties` and `required` both count as declared) — in a node `input:`, the `<route_on>` field a rerouting decision node reads from its escalate agent, a switch case `condition`, a map node's items, and `output_mapping`, but not in a `when:` or a loop `condition`. Only agent nodes are field-checked; a schema built from `allOf`/`oneOf`/`anyOf`/`$ref` is not judged; a node that does not exist inside `coalesce` or `concat` is not an error; an undeclared `workflow.input` field is a warning, not an error — unless it is a near-miss spelling of a declared field (case differences count) or is read through `{{workflow_input.output.<field>}}`, where an input the caller omits does not resolve (it fails a node input or map items, stays as template text in `output_mapping`, and makes a switch case not match); both are errors.
- Workflow node agents should NOT include `ask_user_question` tool — they run autonomously within the workflow.
- When building a workflow, the builder must generate **both** the workflow config AND a separate agent config for each distinct `agent_name` referenced in nodes.

### 2.2 Switch Node

Routes execution to one of several target nodes based on conditions. First matching case wins.

```yaml
- id: route
  type: switch
  depends_on: [classify]            # `category` declared in classify's output schema.
  cases:                            # Required. Evaluated in order.
    - condition: "'{{classify.output.category}}' == 'premium'"
      node: premium_handler         # Target node ID.
    - condition: "'{{classify.output.category}}' == 'standard'"
      node: standard_handler
  default: fallback_handler         # Optional. Target if no case matches.
```

**Switch rules:**
- Cases are evaluated in order — first match wins.
- `condition` uses expr-lang/expr syntax (see Section 6).
- `node` (alias: `then`) specifies the target node ID.
- Target nodes must include the switch node in their `depends_on` array.
- Only the matched target executes; other targets are skipped.
- The switch node's own output is `{selected_branch, selected_case_index, cases_unresolved}`. `selected_branch` is `""` and `selected_case_index` is `-1` when nothing matched and there is no `default`; `cases_unresolved` counts cases that referenced a field no node produced — whether they abstained or answered on the arms that did resolve. Any non-zero count means part of what you wrote is dead; a non-zero count next to an empty `selected_branch` means the switch did not make the decision you wrote at all.
- Use `coalesce` in `output_mapping` to converge results from switch branches (see Section 4).

### 2.3 Map Node

Iterates over a collection, executing a template node for each item in parallel.

```yaml
- id: process_all
  type: map
  depends_on: [split]               # `items` declared in split's output schema.
  node: process_one                 # Required. Template node ID to execute per item.
  items: "{{split.output.items}}"   # Required. Template expression for the collection.
  concurrency_limit: 5              # Optional. Max parallel executions. 0 = unlimited.
  max_items: 100                    # Optional. Safety limit (default 100).
```

The template node receives special variables:
- `{{_map_item}}` — the current item from the collection
- `{{_map_index}}` — the current index (0-based)

```yaml
- id: process_one
  type: agent
  agent_name: ItemProcessor
  input:
    item: "{{_map_item}}"
    index: "{{_map_index}}"
```

**Map rules:**
- The template node (`process_one`) should NOT appear in other nodes' `depends_on` — it's invoked by the map node.
- The map node's output is an array of all template node outputs, in order.
- Set exactly one items source: `items`, `with_param` (alias `withParam`), or `with_items` (alias `withItems`). Each takes a template expression or a literal list; `with_items` is the conventional key for a literal list.
- No other key is accepted — a map node with `items_expression` fails to parse with `requires one of: 'items', 'withParam', or 'withItems'`.

### 2.4 Loop Node

Repeats a body node while a condition is true.

```yaml
- id: refine
  type: loop
  node: refine_step                 # Required. Body node ID to repeat.
  condition: "{{refine_step.output.quality_score}} < 0.9"  # Required. Continue while true.
  max_iterations: 5                 # Optional. Safety limit (default 100).
  delay: "1s"                       # Optional. Delay between iterations.
```

The body node receives:
- `{{_loop_iteration}}` — current iteration counter (0-based)

```yaml
- id: refine_step
  type: agent
  agent_name: Refiner               # `quality_score` and `result` declared in refine_step's output schema.
  input:
    previous: "{{refine_step.output.result}}"
    iteration: "{{_loop_iteration}}"
```

**Loop rules:**
- **Always set `max_iterations`** to prevent infinite loops.
- The condition is checked after each iteration — the body always runs at least once.
- The loop node's output is **not** the body's output. It is `{iterations_completed, stopped_reason}`, where `stopped_reason` is one of `condition_false` (including a condition an omitted `workflow.input` key decided — see §5), `max_iterations` or `condition_unresolved` (the condition referenced a field no node produced). The body's own output is addressed under the **body node's** id.
- The body node should NOT appear in other nodes' `depends_on`.

### 2.5 Workflow Node

Invokes another deployed workflow as a nested sub-workflow.

```yaml
- id: validate
  type: workflow
  workflow_name: ValidationWorkflow  # Required. Must match a deployed workflow.
  depends_on: [prepare]
  input:
    data: "{{prepare.output}}"
```

**Workflow node rules:**
- The referenced workflow must be deployed separately.
- Input/output follows the nested workflow's own `input_schema`/`output_schema`.
- Useful for reusable sub-processes or reducing complexity of large workflows.

### 2.6 Tool Node

Calls a single tool directly — no agent and no LLM in the loop. Use it for a plain, deterministic step (fetch a value, transform data, render a template) where an agent would add nothing.

```yaml
# Tool source declaration: EVERY tool a `type: tool` node invokes must be
# declared — a toolset via `toolsets:`, built-ins, skill tools and MCP tools
# via `tools:`, a platform connector's tools via `connector:` on a node.
toolsets: [WeatherToolset]

nodes:
  - id: fetch_weather
    type: tool
    tool_name: WeatherToolset__get_current_weather  # Required. Its source must be declared above.
    depends_on: [get_city]
    input:                                           # Becomes the tool's arguments.
      city: "{{get_city.output.city}}"
```

**Tool node rules:**
- `tool_name` must match a tool available to the workflow, and that tool's source MUST be declared: toolset tools by listing the toolset in `toolsets:`, built-in tools as a `tools:` entry with `tool_type: builtin`, skill tools as a `tools:` entry with `tool_type: builtin` and the full `<skill>__<tool>` name, MCP tools by `connector: <name>` plus `tool: <server tool name>` when a platform MCP connector exists, otherwise as a `tools:` entry with `tool_type: mcp` and its `connection_params` (see "MCP tool nodes" below), a platform connector's tools by `connector: <name>` on the node (plus optional `tool: <base_name>` to pick one). Give every node that calls a connector tool its own `connector: <name>`. Deploy adds all of that connector's tools to the workflow, but naming one by `tool_name` on another node works only with the exact emitted name — an API connector's operation name (e.g. `get_pet`) or a custom `tool_name` the connector emits as-is. Other connector tools carry a suffix from the connector id (e.g. `sql_query_1a2b3c4d`), so a guessed name passes validation (the connector node already counts as a source) and fails at runtime as an unknown tool. The workflow-level `connectors:` list only declares an inline engine connector (`{name, type, subtype, config}`), never one from the connector store — an entry restating a node's `connector:` is rejected by validation and save, because the engine cannot build it and the workflow would fail at startup. A workflow with `tool_name` tool nodes is rejected by validation and deploy only when it declares no `tools:`, `toolsets:` or `connectors:` and no node binds a `connector:`. A `tool_name` missing from a non-empty declaration fails at runtime with "references unknown tool" — validation does not catch that, so declare every one.
- A `tools:` entry may carry a **`tool_config:`** block — per-tool settings applying to that tool alone, such as a response-size threshold or a response projection. This is where an MCP tool's `extract_fields` goes.
- A tool from an uploaded **toolset** uses its namespaced name (`<Toolset>__<tool>`, e.g. `WeatherToolset__get_current_weather`) and is declared by listing the toolset in the workflow-level `toolsets:` list. This applies only when the prefix is an uploaded toolset — the same `<prefix>__<tool>` shape is used by skill tools (next rule). The platform expands it at deploy into the tool entries, with the toolset's configuration, credentials and approval settings, and redeploys the workflow when the toolset changes. Never hand-write a `tools:` entry for a toolset tool — it is dropped in favour of the expanded entry, and fails deploy as a collision when declared beside a nested `workflow:` block. The Builder cannot create toolsets — they are uploaded on the Toolsets page — so a referenced toolset must already exist on the platform.
- A tool bundled with a **skill** also uses a namespaced name (`<skill>__<tool>`) but is NOT a toolset tool: declare it as a `tools:` entry `{tool_type: builtin, tool_name: <skill>__<tool>}` with the full namespaced name. It resolves at run time through the Secure Tool Runtime that hosts the skill. Never list a skill under `toolsets:` — platform save rejects it as an unknown toolset. When a prefix could be either, check whether it names a skill first. The entry gets **none** of the skill's stored platform config or credentials — workflows do not receive skill config the way an agent with the skill attached does. It works for a skill that needs no platform config; put non-secret values in an inline `tool_config:` on the entry; when the skill needs credentials, use an agent node whose agent has the skill attached instead of a tool node.
- 🛑 **The `<Name>__<tool>` convention is for toolset and skill tools only — never apply it to an MCP tool.** An MCP tool registers under its own server-side name, sanitized, with a prefix added only if the entry sets `tool_name_prefix`. So the `search_repositories` tool on a server you know as `github` registers as **`search_repositories`**, and a node naming `github__search_repositories` fails with "references unknown tool". Copying the toolset prefix onto an MCP tool is the single most common way to author a tool node that deploys cleanly and then cannot run.
- Arguments come from the node's `input:` mapping; the tool's result becomes the node's output, consumable by downstream nodes as `{{<id>.output...}}`.
- No `agent_name` — a tool node runs the tool itself.
- **Describe the tool before you write the node.** Call `describe_tools` with `{tool_name: <name>}` (a built-in, or a `<Toolset>__<tool>` tool) or `{connector: <connector name>, tool: <base name>}` (a connector already on the platform; leave `tool` out to list its tools, up to 50). Take `input:` keys only from the result's `parameters` and `{{<id>.output.<field>}}` references only from its `result`. The preview's `in(...)` and `out(...)` names are enough; `load_artifact` `described_tools.json` for types, descriptions and nested result fields. When the preview ends with `load_artifact described_tools.json for …`, those parts were left out; load it before writing them. `?` means unknown: `in(?)` is parameters unknown, `out(?)` is no result fields declared (`result` is `null`), and `in()` means it takes no parameters. Solace Agent Mesh workflow configuration schema and practical guide. Workflows are DAGs of nodes with deterministic control flow. They publish an agent card and look like any other agent to the system.

For **design guidance** see `sam-workflow-design`. For **agent config** within nodes see `sam-agent-schema`.

## Schema

```yaml
{{SCHEMA:workflow}}
```

---

## 1. Workflow Identity and Required Fields

> **Note:** System fields like `namespace`, `session_service`, and `artifact_service` are injected by the platform at deployment time and must not be included in generated configs.

```yaml
apps:
  - name: my_workflow
    app_config:
      agent_name: my_workflow          # Required. Unique identifier.
      agent_type: workflow             # Required. Must be "workflow".
      description: "..."              # Optional.
      version: "1.0"                  # Optional.
      nodes: [...]                    # Required. At least one node.
      output_mapping: {...}           # Required. Maps workflow output.
```

**Rules:**
- `agent_type: workflow` is required — this is what distinguishes a workflow from an agent.
- `agent_name` must be unique across the deployment, same as agents. Convention: `snake_case`.
- `nodes` and `output_mapping` are both required — a workflow must have at least one node and must define how its output is constructed.

---

## 2. Node Types

Every node has `id` (unique within the workflow) and `type`. Different types require different fields.

### 2.1 Agent Node

Invokes a deployed agent. The most common node type.

```yaml
- id: analyze
  type: agent
  agent_name: Analyzer              # Required. Must match a deployed agent.
  depends_on: [extract]             # Nodes that must complete first.
  input:                            # Data passed to the agent. Values can be templates.
    data: "{{extract.output.text}}" # `extract` declares `text` and `has_data` in its output schema (its agent's
                                    # `output_schema` or an `output_schema_override` on the `extract` node).
  instruction: "Focus on security issues only."  # Optional. Appended to agent's instruction.
  timeout: "2m"                     # Optional. Overrides default_node_timeout.
  when: "'{{extract.output.has_data}}' == 'true'"  # Optional. Skip if false. `has_data` is declared by `extract`.
  retry_strategy:                   # Optional. Overrides workflow-level retry.
    limit: 2
    retry_policy: OnError
  input_schema_override: {...}      # Optional. Override agent's input_schema for this invocation.
  output_schema_override: {...}     # Optional. Override agent's output_schema for this invocation.
```

**Agent node requirements:**
- The agent referenced by `agent_name` must be deployed separately as its own agent config.
- Workflow node agents should use `supports_streaming: false` and define `output_schema` so the workflow can reliably consume structured output.
- 🛑 **Reference `{{<id>.output.<field>}}` only for a field the node declares** — in its `output_schema_override` or its agent's `output_schema` — and make the agent's `instruction` (or the node's `instruction`) tell it to return exactly those keys. An agent node that declares no output schema guarantees no fields: its output is whatever structured result the agent returned, else `{"text": "..."}` — so not even `text` is guaranteed: an agent that returns a structured result has no `text`. When the shape is not declared, bind the whole `{{<id>.output}}` in `output_mapping` or a node `input:`; a switch case or a map node's `items` needs a field, so declare it. To add a field to a node that already has a schema, extend that schema — a new `output_schema_override` replaces the agent's whole schema. This applies to `output_mapping`, node `input:`, `when:`, switch/loop conditions and the `<route_on>` field a rerouting decision node reads from its escalate target alike. Build validation (`validate_build_manifest` with `full_validation: true`) rejects a field reference into an agent node in the build that declares no output schema, and a field outside the schema it does declare (`properties` and `required` both count as declared) — in a node `input:`, the `<route_on>` field a rerouting decision node reads from its escalate agent, a switch case `condition`, a map node's items, and `output_mapping`, but not in a `when:` or a loop `condition`. Only agent nodes are field-checked; a schema built from `allOf`/`oneOf`/`anyOf`/`$ref` is not judged; a node that does not exist inside `coalesce` or `concat` is not an error; an undeclared `workflow.input` field is a warning, not an error — unless it is a near-miss spelling of a declared field (case differences count) or is read through `{{workflow_input.output.<field>}}`, where an input the caller omits does not resolve (it fails a node input or map items, stays as template text in `output_mapping`, and makes a switch case not match); both are errors.
- Workflow node agents should NOT include `ask_user_question` tool — they run autonomously within the workflow.
- When building a workflow, the builder must generate **both** the workflow config AND a separate agent config for each distinct `agent_name` referenced in nodes.

### 2.2 Switch Node

Routes execution to one of several target nodes based on conditions. First matching case wins.

```yaml
- id: route
  type: switch
  depends_on: [classify]            # `category` declared in classify's output schema.
  cases:                            # Required. Evaluated in order.
    - condition: "'{{classify.output.category}}' == 'premium'"
      node: premium_handler         # Target node ID.
    - condition: "'{{classify.output.category}}' == 'standard'"
      node: standard_handler
  default: fallback_handler         # Optional. Target if no case matches.
```

**Switch rules:**
- Cases are evaluated in order — first match wins.
- `condition` uses expr-lang/expr syntax (see Section 6).
- `node` (alias: `then`) specifies the target node ID.
- Target nodes must include the switch node in their `depends_on` array.
- Only the matched target executes; other targets are skipped.
- The switch node's own output is `{selected_branch, selected_case_index, cases_unresolved}`. `selected_branch` is `""` and `selected_case_index` is `-1` when nothing matched and there is no `default`; `cases_unresolved` counts cases that referenced a field no node produced — whether they abstained or answered on the arms that did resolve. Any non-zero count means part of what you wrote is dead; a non-zero count next to an empty `selected_branch` means the switch did not make the decision you wrote at all.
- Use `coalesce` in `output_mapping` to converge results from switch branches (see Section 4).

### 2.3 Map Node

Iterates over a collection, executing a template node for each item in parallel.

```yaml
- id: process_all
  type: map
  depends_on: [split]               # `items` declared in split's output schema.
  node: process_one                 # Required. Template node ID to execute per item.
  items: "{{split.output.items}}"   # Required. Template expression for the collection.
  concurrency_limit: 5              # Optional. Max parallel executions. 0 = unlimited.
  max_items: 100                    # Optional. Safety limit (default 100).
```

The template node receives special variables:
- `{{_map_item}}` — the current item from the collection
- `{{_map_index}}` — the current index (0-based)

```yaml
- id: process_one
  type: agent
  agent_name: ItemProcessor
  input:
    item: "{{_map_item}}"
    index: "{{_map_index}}"
```

**Map rules:**
- The template node (`process_one`) should NOT appear in other nodes' `depends_on` — it's invoked by the map node.
- The map node's output is an array of all template node outputs, in order.
- Set exactly one items source: `items`, `with_param` (alias `withParam`), or `with_items` (alias `withItems`). Each takes a template expression or a literal list; `with_items` is the conventional key for a literal list.
- No other key is accepted — a map node with `items_expression` fails to parse with `requires one of: 'items', 'withParam', or 'withItems'`.

### 2.4 Loop Node

Repeats a body node while a condition is true.

```yaml
- id: refine
  type: loop
  node: refine_step                 # Required. Body node ID to repeat.
  condition: "{{refine_step.output.quality_score}} < 0.9"  # Required. Continue while true.
  max_iterations: 5                 # Optional. Safety limit (default 100).
  delay: "1s"                       # Optional. Delay between iterations.
```

The body node receives:
- `{{_loop_iteration}}` — current iteration counter (0-based)

```yaml
- id: refine_step
  type: agent
  agent_name: Refiner               # `quality_score` and `result` declared in refine_step's output schema.
  input:
    previous: "{{refine_step.output.result}}"
    iteration: "{{_loop_iteration}}"
```

**Loop rules:**
- **Always set `max_iterations`** to prevent infinite loops.
- The condition is checked after each iteration — the body always runs at least once.
- The loop node's output is **not** the body's output. It is `{iterations_completed, stopped_reason}`, where `stopped_reason` is one of `condition_false` (including a condition an omitted `workflow.input` key decided — see §5), `max_iterations` or `condition_unresolved` (the condition referenced a field no node produced). The body's own output is addressed under the **body node's** id.
- The body node should NOT appear in other nodes' `depends_on`.

### 2.5 Workflow Node

Invokes another deployed workflow as a nested sub-workflow.

```yaml
- id: validate
  type: workflow
  workflow_name: ValidationWorkflow  # Required. Must match a deployed workflow.
  depends_on: [prepare]
  input:
    data: "{{prepare.output}}"
```

**Workflow node rules:**
- The referenced workflow must be deployed separately.
- Input/output follows the nested workflow's own `input_schema`/`output_schema`.
- Useful for reusable sub-processes or reducing complexity of large workflows.

### 2.6 Tool Node

Calls a single tool directly — no agent and no LLM in the loop. Use it for a plain, deterministic step (fetch a value, transform data, render a template) where an agent would add nothing.

```yaml
# declared — a toolset via `toolsets:`, built-ins, skill tools and MCP tools
# via `tools:`, a platform connector's tools via `connector:` on a node.
toolsets: [WeatherToolset]

nodes:
  - id: fetch_weather
    type: tool
    tool_name: WeatherToolset__get_current_weather  # Required. Its source must be declared above.
    depends_on: [get_city]
```

# Document Conversion Skill

You are a document conversion specialist. For any conversion task, follow the decision tree below to pick exactly **one** tool per call. Do not invent tools, chain unrelated conversions, or fall back to unsupported operations.

The tools listed below are top-level STR tools on the agent, not bundled by this skill. This skill exists to help you **pick the right one**.

## Decision tree

Given an **input artifact** (or raw text) and a desired **target**, evaluate in order and stop at the first match:

1. **Input and target are both PDF** (no visual content change — just page-level operations: merge, split, extract a page range, rotate, text watermark, encrypt/decrypt, inspect metadata)
   → use `pdf_ops`.

2. **Target is `markdown`** (LLM-friendly text extraction from PDF/DOCX/XLSX/PPTX/HTML/CSV/EPUB/IPYNB)
   → use `convert_file_to_markdown` if available on this agent. It is the purpose-built path and produces much cleaner Markdown than anything via LibreOffice.

3. **Input is Mermaid source** (a string beginning with `graph`, `flowchart`, `sequenceDiagram`, `classDiagram`, `stateDiagram`, `erDiagram`, `gantt`, `pie`, `journey`, `gitGraph`, etc.) **and target is an image** (SVG/PNG)
   → use `mermaid_diagram_generator`.

4. **Input is text/Markdown/plain prose and target is audio (MP3)**
   - Single narrator → use `text_to_speech`.
   - Dialogue/script with multiple named speakers → use `multi_speaker_text_to_speech`.
   - Both require `GEMINI_API_KEY` in tool configuration; if absent, the tool returns a clean error and you should tell the user.

5. **You have multiple audio artifacts and need to stitch them together** (e.g., concatenating TTS segments with pauses)
   → use `concatenate_audio`.

6. **Input or target is audio/video** (mp3, wav, flac, mp4, mov, webm, m4a, mkv, opus, aac, etc.) — format conversions, transcoding, trimming, extract audio from video, stitch a video from images
   → use `ffmpeg`. For probing (`-show_format`, `-show_streams`) use `ffprobe`.

7. **Target is PPTX and the source is Markdown, a bullet outline, or a structured slide spec** (i.e., you're *generating* a new presentation, not just bridging office formats)
   - Use `pptx_create_presentation`. Map the content onto per-slide layouts (headings → title/section, bullet groups → bullet_list, tables → table); for raw Markdown, translate its structure rather than dumping it verbatim.
   - (Use `libreoffice_convert` instead when converting an *existing* DOCX/ODP/HTML file to PPTX.)

8. **You need to SEE the rendered appearance of a document or deck** — to visually inspect/verify the layout of a presentation or document you (or the user) produced, preview each page, or "look at" the output before delivering it
   → use `render_document_to_images`. It renders a pptx/docx/xlsx/odp/html/pdf to one PNG **per page**, then you call `load_artifact` on each page PNG to view it directly. This is the right tool for "check that my slides look right" — prefer it over `image_magick` for multi-page documents (image_magick PDF→PNG and `libreoffice_convert` pptx→png only give you the first page).

9. **Input and target are both images**, OR input is a PDF and target is a single raster/vector image the *user asked for as output* (PDF→PNG, PDF→JPG, SVG→PNG, image resize/crop/annotate)
   → use `image_magick`.

10. **Input is HTML and target is PDF**
   → use `html_to_pdf`. LibreOffice has no export filter for HTML to PDF, so `libreoffice_convert` fails on it.

11. **Input or target is an office document, text format, EPUB, or HTML**, OR the conversion needs a format bridge that LibreOffice understands (e.g., DOCX↔PDF, PPTX↔PDF, XLSX↔CSV, HTML↔DOCX, TXT↔PDF, RTF↔PDF, EPUB export)
   → use `libreoffice_convert`.

If none of the above matches, stop and tell the user the conversion is not supported by any of your tools.

## Format matrix (common pairs)

| From ↓ / To → | PDF | DOCX | PPTX | XLSX | HTML | TXT | CSV | Markdown | PNG/JPG | MP4 | EPUB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PDF** | `pdf_ops` | libreoffice_convert | libreoffice_convert | — | libreoffice_convert | libreoffice_convert | — | convert_file_to_markdown | image_magick | — | libreoffice_convert |
| **DOCX** | libreoffice_convert | — | libreoffice_convert | — | libreoffice_convert | libreoffice_convert | — | convert_file_to_markdown | libreoffice_convert → image_magick | — | libreoffice_convert |
| **PPTX** | libreoffice_convert | libreoffice_convert | — | — | libreoffice_convert | libreoffice_convert | — | convert_file_to_markdown | render_document_to_images (per page) | — | — |
| **XLSX** | libreoffice_convert | — | — | — | libreoffice_convert | — | libreoffice_convert | convert_file_to_markdown | — | — | — |
| **HTML** | html_to_pdf | libreoffice_convert | — | — | — | libreoffice_convert | — | convert_file_to_markdown | render_document_to_images (per page) | — | libreoffice_convert |
| **TXT** | libreoffice_convert | libreoffice_convert | — | — | libreoffice_convert | — | — | (passthrough) | — | — | libreoffice_convert |
| **CSV** | libreoffice_convert | — | — | libreoffice_convert | libreoffice_convert | libreoffice_convert | — | convert_file_to_markdown | — | — | — |
| **Image** | image_magick (via PDF encoder) | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | image_magick | ffmpeg (image→video) | — |
| **Audio/Video** | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | ffmpeg (extract frame) | ffmpeg | — |

A dash means there is no single-step path. For two-step paths (e.g., DOCX → PNG via PDF) call `libreoffice_convert` to produce an intermediate PDF and then `image_magick` to rasterize it.

## Common workflows

- **DOCX/PPTX/XLSX → PDF**: `libreoffice_convert` with `target_format: "pdf"`.
- **PDF → PNG (page as image)**: `image_magick` with `command: "{input[0]}[0] -density 150 {output}"` and `output_filename: "page1.png"`. Use `[N]` to pick a specific page.
- **Merge multiple PDFs**: `pdf_ops` with `operation: "merge"` — pass the first as `input_pdf` and the rest in `additional_pdfs`.
- **Split a PDF into single pages**: `pdf_ops` with `operation: "split"`.
- **Extract PDF pages 2-4**: `pdf_ops` with `operation: "extract_pages"` and `page_range: "2-4"`.
- **Add a draft watermark**: `pdf_ops` with `operation: "watermark"`, `watermark_text: "DRAFT"`.
- **Encrypt a PDF with a password**: `pdf_ops` with `operation: "encrypt"`, `password: "<pw>"`.
- **Inspect a PDF**: `pdf_ops` with `operation: "info"` returns a JSON summary (page count, version, encrypted, metadata).
- **CSV → XLSX**: `libreoffice_convert` with `target_format: "xlsx"`.
- **Any document → Markdown**: `convert_file_to_markdown` if available. Otherwise, prefer `libreoffice_convert` to HTML → then the agent can present the text.
- **Markdown / outline / slide spec → PPTX (generate a new deck)**: `pptx_create_presentation`. Map the content onto per-slide layouts (titles, bullets, tables, charts, images); for raw Markdown, translate its structure into layouts rather than dumping it verbatim.
- **Existing DOCX/ODP → PPTX (format bridge, preserve layout)**: `libreoffice_convert` with `target_format: "pptx"`. (Not `pptx_*` — those generate new decks.)
- **Narrate a block of text as an MP3**: `text_to_speech`. For a multi-voice dialogue, use `multi_speaker_text_to_speech` and label each line with a speaker.
- **Glue together multiple audio clips (e.g., TTS segments + pauses)**: `concatenate_audio` with the clips in the desired order.
- **Mermaid source → diagram image**: `mermaid_diagram_generator` with the Mermaid text and desired format (SVG or PNG).
- **Visually inspect / preview a generated deck or document**: `render_document_to_images` → then `load_artifact` on each page PNG to see it. Use this to confirm a `pptx_create_presentation` deck (or any document) is laid out correctly before delivering it.
- **Scanned PDF → searchable text**: **OCR is out of scope.** If the user needs OCR, tell them so explicitly. You can often *read* the image content yourself via multimodal vision — render the pages with `render_document_to_images` (one PNG per page) and `load_artifact` each, and the runtime will show them to you.
- **Video → audio track**: `ffmpeg` with `-i {input[0]} -vn -acodec libmp3lame {output}` and `output_filename: "audio.mp3"`.
- **Inspect an audio/video file**: `ffprobe` — returns format metadata, stream list, duration, codecs.

## Tool cheat sheets (summary)

See the tool schemas for full parameter lists. These are the typical shapes you need.

### `libreoffice_convert`
```yaml
input_document: <artifact>
target_format: "pdf" | "docx" | "odt" | "pptx" | "xlsx" | "csv" | "html" | "txt" | "epub" | "png" | "svg" | "rtf"
output_filename: "optional — defaults to <input-basename>.<target_format>"
filter: "optional — advanced LibreOffice export filter string"
timeout_seconds: 120  # default
```

### `pdf_ops`
```yaml
operation: "merge" | "split" | "extract_pages" | "rotate" | "watermark" | "encrypt" | "decrypt" | "info"
input_pdf: <artifact>
additional_pdfs: [<artifact>, ...]   # merge only
page_range: "1-3,5,7-"               # extract_pages (required) / rotate (optional)
rotation: 90 | 180 | 270              # rotate (required)
watermark_text: "DRAFT"               # watermark (required)
watermark_opts: "font:Helvetica,points:24,opacity:0.3,rotation:45"  # watermark (optional)
password: "..."                       # encrypt/decrypt (required)
output_filename: "optional"
```

### `image_magick`
Full ImageMagick arguments to `magick`. Use `{input[0]}`, `{output}`, `{output_dir}` placeholders.

### `ffmpeg`
Full FFmpeg arguments (without the `ffmpeg` prefix; `-y` is added automatically). Use the same placeholders as `image_magick`.

### `ffprobe`
Same placeholder convention as `ffmpeg`. Typical invocation: `-v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams {input[0]}`.

### `pptx_create_presentation`
Save the slide array as a YAML/JSON artifact first, then pass its filename as `slides`. Each slide picks a `layout` (title, section, bullet_list, comparison, big_number, timeline, icon_grid, table, chart, quote, image_*, closing). Title/body/bullet text supports inline markdown (`**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``).
```yaml
# 1. save_artifact "deck-spec.yaml":
- layout: title
  title: "Overview"
- layout: bullet_list
  title: "Highlights"
  bullets: ["**Point A:** detail", "Point B"]
# 2. call the tool:
title: "My Deck"
slides: "deck-spec.yaml"
output_name: "deck"
# The deck look is set by tool_config on the agent (template_profile): neutral
# by default (no logo), solace_2025 for the Solace brand, none for plain slides.
```

### `render_document_to_images`
```yaml
input_document: <artifact>   # pptx/docx/xlsx/odp/odt/ods/html/pdf
dpi: 150            # optional, render resolution
pages: "2-4"        # optional — "N", "N-M", or "N-"; default all pages
max_pages: 50       # optional cap
# Produces one PNG artifact per page (<doc>-page-<N>.png).
# Then call load_artifact on each page PNG to view it as a vision attachment.
```

### `text_to_speech`
```yaml
text: "Hello, world."
voice: "optional voice name, or omit"
# Gender/tone params are optional; see the tool schema for the full list.
# Requires GEMINI_API_KEY at invocation time.
```

### `multi_speaker_text_to_speech`
```yaml
conversation_text: |
  Alice: Hi there.
  Bob: Hello Alice.
speakers:
  - name: "Alice"
    voice: "en-US-Wavenet-A"
  - name: "Bob"
    voice: "en-US-Wavenet-B"
# Requires GEMINI_API_KEY.
```

### `concatenate_audio`
```yaml
clips_to_join:
  - artifact: <audio artifact 1>
    pause_after_seconds: 0.5
  - artifact: <audio artifact 2>
output_filename: "combined.mp3"
```

### `mermaid_diagram_generator`
```yaml
mermaid_source: "graph TD\nA --> B\nB --> C"
output_format: "svg" | "png"
output_filename: "diagram.svg"
```

## Load-order notes

- If your instruction mentions "PDF operations" or "merge/split/rotate/watermark" **always** go to `pdf_ops` — these verbs are never best served by `libreoffice_convert` or `image_magick`.
- If the user says "flatten" or "rasterize" a PDF, use `image_magick` to render the PDF as images.
- `libreoffice_convert` is a single-input / single-output tool. For multi-document workflows, chain separate calls.
- All tools respect a 200 MiB per-output-file cap. If you exceed it, tell the user and suggest splitting the work.

## References

- `references/format-matrix.md` — extended source/target lookup table.
- `references/libreoffice-filters.md` — advanced `soffice` export filter strings.
- `references/pdfcpu-recipes.md` — pdfcpu page-range syntax and watermark option strings.

See the tool schemas for full parameter lists. These are the typical shapes you need.

### `libreoffice_convert`
```yaml
input_document: <artifact>
target_format: "pdf" | "docx" | "odt" | "pptx" | "xlsx" | "csv" | "html" | "txt" | "epub" | "png" | "svg" | "rtf"
output_filename: "optional — defaults to <input-basename>.<target_format>"
filter: "optional — advanced LibreOffice export filter string"
timeout_seconds: 120  # default
```

### `pdf_ops`
```yaml
operation: "merge" | "split" | "extract_pages" | "rotate" | "watermark" | "encrypt" | "decrypt" | "info"
input_pdf: <artifact>
additional_pdfs: [<artifact>, ...]   # merge only
page_range: "1-3,5,7-"               # extract_pages (required) / rotate (optional)
rotation: 90 | 180 | 270              # rotate (required)
watermark_text: "DRAFT"               # watermark (required)
watermark_opts: "font:Helvetica,points:24,opacity:0.3,rotation:45"  # watermark (optional)
password: "..."                       # encrypt/decrypt (required)
output_filename: "optional"
```

### `image_magick`
Full ImageMagick arguments to `magick`. Use `{input[0]}`, `{output}`, `{output_dir}` placeholders.

### `ffmpeg`
Full FFmpeg arguments (without the `ffmpeg` prefix; `-y` is added automatically). Use the same placeholders as `image_magick`.

### `ffprobe`
Same placeholder convention as `ffmpeg`. Typical invocation: `-v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams {input[0]}`.

### `pptx_create_presentation`
Save the slide array as a YAML/JSON artifact first, then pass its filename as `slides`. Each slide picks a `layout` (title, section, bullet_list, comparison, big_number, timeline, icon_grid, table, chart, quote, image_*, closing). Title/body/bullet text supports inline markdown (`**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``).
```yaml
# 1. save_artifact "deck-spec.yaml":
- layout: title
  title: "Overview"
- layout: bullet_list
  title: "Highlights"
  bullets: ["**Point A:** detail", "Point B"]
# 2. call the tool:
title: "My Deck"
slides: "deck-spec.yaml"
output_name: "deck"
# The deck look is set by tool_config on the agent (template_profile): neutral
# by default (no logo), solace_2025 for the Solace brand, none for plain slides.
```

### `render_document_to_images`
```yaml
input_document: <artifact>   # pptx/docx/xlsx/odp/odt/ods/html/pdf
dpi: 150            # optional, render resolution
pages: "2-4"        # optional — "N", "N-M", or "N-"; default all pages
max_pages: 50       # optional cap
# Produces one PNG artifact per page (<doc>-page-<N>.png).
# Then call load_artifact on each page PNG to view it as a vision attachment.
```

### `text_to_speech`
```yaml
text: "Hello, world."
voice: "optional voice name, or omit"
# Gender/tone params are optional; see the tool schema for the full list.
# Requires GEMINI_API_KEY at invocation time.
```

### `multi_speaker_text_to_speech`
```yaml
conversation_text: |
  Alice: Hi there.
  Bob: Hello Alice.
speakers:
  - name: "Alice"
    voice: "en-US-Wavenet-A"
  - name: "Bob"
    voice: "en-US-Wavenet-B"
# Requires GEMINI_API_KEY.
```

### `concatenate_audio`
```yaml
clips_to_join:
  - artifact: <audio artifact 1>
    pause_after_seconds: 0.5
  - artifact: <audio artifact 2>
output_filename: "combined.mp3"
```

### `mermaid_diagram_generator`
```yaml
mermaid_source: "graph TD\nA --> B\nB --> C"
output_format: "svg" | "png"
output_filename: "diagram.svg"
```

## Load-order notes

- If your instruction mentions "PDF operations" or "merge/split/rotate/watermark" **always** go to `pdf_ops` — these verbs are never best served by `libreoffice_convert` or `image_magick`.
- If the user says "flatten" or "rasterize" a PDF, use `image_magick` to render the PDF as images.
- `libreoffice_convert` is a single-input / single-output tool. For multi-document workflows, chain separate calls.
- All tools respect a 200 MiB per-output-file cap. If you exceed it, tell the user and suggest splitting the work.
